system.specialDefenses: Can be hit only by magic weapons
system.description:
A semi-intelligent kind of air elemental, normally invisible. It is usually met only when a cleric conjures one, though they also roam the ethereal and astral planes, where they can be dimly seen.

  • Strength and speed: it does not fight as such, but it is extremely strong and very fast. It can carry more than 10,000 gold pieces of weight, and it travels at twice the speed of an invisible stalker.
  • Grasp: a creature it grabs needs 18 strength to have any chance of breaking free. The chance equals the percentage of exceptional strength: a human with 18/50 strength has a 50% chance, and 18/00 or 19 breaks free automatically.
  • Surprise: on the physical plane it surprises on 1-4 (out of 6).
  • Frustrated: if it is prevented from finishing its assigned mission, it goes insane, returns to the cleric who sent it, and attacks as a double strength invisible stalker. It usually attacks the same way if met ethereally or astrally.

For more details, see the cleric spell aerial servant.

The anhkheg burrows through the earth like an earthworm, preferring soil rich in minerals and organic matter, so it is usually found in forests and good farmland. Farmers dread it, because it adds fresh meat, human or otherwise, to its diet of soil.

  • Ambush: its favorite tactic is to lie 5-10 feet underground until its antennae sense a likely victim passing overhead, then burrow straight up beneath it and grab it.
  • Bite: its mouth cannot rip and tear, so its mandibles crush the prey and secrete a digestive enzyme that does an extra 1-4 points per turn until the prey is completely dissolved.
  • Acid squirt: if hard pressed in battle, it can squirt its digestive acid 30 feet, once per six hours. This does 8-32 hit points of damage to the creature struck, or half if it makes its saving throw. Afterward the anhkheg cannot digest anything for the same length of time, so it usually prefers to bite.

Description: a brownish chitinous shell, a pinkish underside, and glistening black eyes.

Giant ants met in the open are 90% likely to be just workers.

  • Nest: in their lair there are double the number rolled, plus 1 warrior ant for every 5 workers. The egg chamber is guarded by 5-50 workers and 5 warriors. Any treasure is in the queen’s chamber. Giant ant eggs have no normal market value.
  • Warrior ant: 3 hit dice. Its mandibles do 2-8 hit points; if they hit, it also tries to sting for 3-12 points. A victim stung must save versus poison; on a success he or she takes only 1-4 hit points.
  • Queen: 10 hit dice, but she neither moves nor attacks. If she is killed, the other ants become confused (as the spell) for six melee rounds and then leave the nest.

The typical ape lives only in lonely tropical forests. It is shy and not aggressive, but fights fiercely if threatened or cornered. If both of its hands hit, it does an extra 1-6 points by grabbing and rending its opponent.

A larger, stronger, and very aggressive relative of the gorilla, with fair intelligence (IQ 70+) and great cunning. It particularly hungers for human flesh.

  • Senses: keen sight, hearing, and smell, so it is surprised only on a roll of 1.
  • Rending: if both hands hit, it does an extra 1-8 hit points of rending damage.
Axe beaks are prehistoric flightless birds that eat meat. They are very fast runners and hunt aggressively by day. The lower body looks like an ostrich’s, with a strong neck and a heavy, sharp beak.

Baboons are mainly plant-eating animals that live in groups. A tribe is led by 2-8 large males (+1 hit point of damage on their attacks). Half the tribe is young, who do not attack. The baboons try to drive off anyone who invades their home territory, but the tribe is 90% likely to flee if met with determined resistance.

These burrowing animals usually live alone. Their speed gives them their good armor class. They are fierce fighters and defend their territory stoutly. If more than 1 is met, it is a mated pair (with young). A badger pelt typically sells for 10-30 gold pieces.

Giant badger: a very rare kind that grows to twice normal size: hit dice 3; damage 1-3/1-3/1-6; size M. Otherwise identical.

A prehistoric ancestor of the rhinoceros: a huge plant-eating mammal that tends to charge anything nearby to trample it. Two met together are a mated pair; if three are met, the third is a young one (roll percentile dice for its size).

Barracuda live in warm salt water. These predatory fish are lightning quick, going from standing still to full speed in a single melee round. They attack any prey that is injured, looks helpless, or is fairly small.

A reptilian monster with eight legs, but so slow a metabolism that it moves only slowly. It is usually dull brown with a yellowish underbelly, and its eyes glow pale green.

  • Gaze: its strong, toothy jaws are less dangerous than its gaze, which turns to stone any fleshly creature that meets its glance.
  • Reflection: if its gaze is reflected so that it sees its own eyes, the basilisk itself is petrified. This needs light at least as bright as bright torchlight and a good, smooth reflector.
  • Other planes: it can see into both the astral and ethereal planes. On the astral plane its gaze kills; on the ethereal plane it turns victims to ethereal stone, visible only to those on that plane or able to see ethereal objects.

All bears eat both plants and meat, though the gigantic cave bear prefers meat. All have excellent hearing and smell but rather poor eyesight. The size shown is the average for each kind; larger individuals are correspondingly more powerful.

  • Temper: black bears are usually not aggressive; brown bears are; cave bears are quite aggressive. The grizzly bear is a very aggressive brown bear.
  • Hug: if a bear’s paw hits with a roll of 18 or better, it also hugs for the extra damage shown.
  • Fighting on: brown and cave bears keep fighting for 1-4 melee rounds after reaching 0 to −8 hit points. At −9 or lower they die at once.

These intelligent but docile creatures flee any attack if they can, but fight fiercely if cornered or if their huge lodge is threatened.

  • Home: they live in a lake made by their vast dam. In its middle they build a veritable castle of mud and logs, with walls at least 5’ thick, where the whole community lives. When the alarm is sounded (a tail slap on the water), every beaver rushes there to defend it and the young.
  • Young: there is one young beaver for every adult (roll percentile dice for size).
  • Trade: giant beavers sometimes trade. For coins or other valuables they can sometimes be persuaded to build dam-like structures, if there is water near the site, since they work in and from water. They especially prize certain barks and tender twigs, notably birch, aspen, and willow.
  • Value: their hides are worth 500 to 2,000 gold pieces each. Kits of under 8 hit points can be subdued, captured, and sold for 100 to 200 gold pieces per hit point.

All giant beetles are basically unintelligent and always hungry. They eat almost any organic material, including other beetles. They taste with their antennae or feelers; if something is organic, they grasp it with their mandibles, crush it, and eat it. Because of this thorough grinding, nothing actually eaten by a giant beetle can be revived by any means short of a wish. They hear and see poorly and rely mainly on taste and feel.

Bombardier beetle: usually found above ground in wooded areas. It feeds mainly on offal and carrion, gathering huge heaps of it to lay its eggs in.

  • Vapor: if attacked or disturbed, there is a 50% chance each melee round that it turns its rear toward its attacker(s) and fires an 8’ × 8’ × 8’ cloud of reeking, reddish acid vapor, doing 3-12 hit points of damage to every creature inside. It can do this every third melee round, but no more than twice in eight hours.
  • Noise: the sound of the release has a 20% chance of stunning each creature with hearing within a 16’ radius, and the same chance of deafening each one there that was not stunned. Stunning lasts 2-8 melee rounds, followed by 2-8 more melee rounds of deafness. Deafening lasts 2-12 melee rounds.

Boring beetle: it feeds on rotting wood and similar material, so it is usually found inside huge trees or in unused underground tunnel complexes. Underground it grows molds, slimes, and fungi for food, starting the cultures on decaying plant and animal matter and wastes. Individually they are no smarter than other beetles, but groups are rumored to develop a communal intelligence with consciousness and reasoning close to a human brain’s.

Fire beetle: the smallest giant beetle, but its powerful mandibles can still do serious damage. Found above and below ground, mostly active at night. Two glands above its eyes and one near the back of its abdomen glow red. Miners and adventurers prize them, because the glands keep glowing for 1-6 days after being removed, lighting a 10’ radius.

Rhinoceros beetle: this uncommon monster roams tropical and subtropical jungles looking for fruit and vegetation, crushing anything in its path. Its horn extends about 6’.

Stag beetle: these woodland beetles love grain and similar crops, so they sometimes become serious pests and raid farmland. Like other beetles they see and hear poorly, but they fight if attacked, and attack anything organic they consider food. Their two horns are usually at least 8’ long.

Water beetle: found only in fresh water at least 30’ deep. These voracious eaters prey on almost any animal but will eat nearly anything. Slow and ponderous on land, they move very fast in water. They hunt by scent and vibration.

The beholder (eye tyrant, sphere of many eyes) is usually found underground, though it sometimes lairs in desolate wilderness. Its globe-shaped body floats slowly about by levitation. On top are 10 eyestalks; in the middle are a great eleventh eye and a large mouth full of pointed teeth.

  • Armor: the body has a hard chitinous covering (AC 2). The eyestalks and eyes are less well protected (AC 7).
  • Damage: eyestalks do not count toward its hit points, and lost ones grow back (1 week per stalk). Each eyestalk takes 8 to 12 hit points before being lost. The body can take two-thirds of the total hit points and the central eye one-third: a beholder with 45 hit points dies after 30 points of damage to its body, and its eleventh eye stops working after 15.
  • Hit location: the body is 75% of the target area, the central eye and the eyestalks 10% each, and the 10 small eyes 5%.

Eyes: each eye has a different function. Against attacks from a 90° arc in front of it, usually only the central eye and 1-4 eyestalks can work. Against attacks from 180°, double the number of eyestalks; from 270° or 360°, triple or quadruple it. Against attacks from above, all 10 eyestalks work, but the central eye cannot. The functions are:

1 Charm person spell6 Disintegrate ray (2” range)
2 Charm monster spell7 Fear (as a wand)
3 Sleep spell8 Slow spell
4 Telekinese 2,500 GP wt.9 Cause serious wound (5” range)
5 Flesh-stone ray (3” range)10 Death ray (4” range)

11 Anti-magic ray (14” range)

Nature: beholders are hateful, aggressive, and greedy, and usually attack at once. Facing a particularly powerful party, there is a 50% chance one will listen to negotiation: either to be bribed not to attack, or to demand a ransom for not attacking, depending on the strength of the other side. They speak their own language and the tongue of lawful evil creatures.
system.hpNote: Eyestalks do not count toward its hit points. The body takes two-thirds of the total and the central eye one-third (MM p.10). The hit dice it attacks as are not given.

system.specialDefenses: Blows, cold and lightning do not harm
system.sizeText: S to L (5’ dia. to 8’ dia.)
system.description:
The black pudding is a monster made up of groups of single cells, a scavenger and hunter normally found only underground. It can flow through narrow openings (such as a 1” crack under a door), and moves as well on walls and ceilings as on floors. It sometimes varies in color; grey, brown, and white are not uncommon.

  • Attack: its tiny mouths and saliva do 3-24 hit points of damage per melee round to exposed flesh.
  • Wood: to get at food it can eat through about two inches of wood, over an area equal to its diameter, in 1 melee round.
  • Metal: its corrosive saliva dissolves chainmail in 1 melee round and plate mail in 2, plus 1 more melee round for each plus of magical armor. So +1 magic plate armor must touch a black pudding for 3 melee rounds before it dissolves.
  • Splitting: chopping, striking, or lightning breaks it into two or more parts, each able to attack.
  • Cold and fire: cold does not affect it. Fire does normal damage, and puddings avoid flames.
  • Size: 10-20 hit points, about 5’ across; 21-40, 6’; 41-60, 7’; 61-80, 8’. Even the smallest (down to 1’ across) do normal damage, because larger puddings simply cannot bring all their mouths to bear.

These brown and yellowish creatures are as intelligent as normal humans, with a fairly complex language of barks, yaps, whines, and growls. They can use a limited form of teleportation, the blink.

  • Blinking in combat: pack members blink in and out at random. An individual teleports on a 7 or better on d12. Roll again for where it reappears: 1 = in front of the opponent, 2 = shielded (or left) front flank, 3 = unshielded (or right) front flank, 4-12 = behind. It reappears 1’ to 3’ from the opponent and can attack at once. (Overall, a teleporting blink dog has a 75% chance of appearing behind its opponent.) Blinking is an inborn instinct and never puts the animal into a space already filled by a solid object.
  • Retreat: if seriously threatened, or after losing 25% or more, the whole pack blinks out and does not return.
  • Enemies: blink dogs and displacer beasts hate each other and always attack each other.
  • Pups: in the lair there is a 50% chance of 3-12 pups (1-2 hit dice, 1-2/1-3 hit points damage per attack). They are worth 1,000 to 2,000 gold pieces on the market, since they can be tamed and trained.

These are pig-like animals that eat both plants and meat. Only the warthog is limited to warmer climates.

Wild boar: if more than 1 is met, the rest are sows (3 hit dice, 2-8 hit points damage per attack) and young, in a ratio of 1 sow to 4 young. So a group of 12 has 1 boar, 3 sows, and 8 young. The boar fights on for 2-5 melee rounds after reaching 0 to −6 hit points, but dies at once at −7 or lower.

Giant boar (elothere): this very aggressive prehistoric forerunner of the wild boar. If 3 or more are met, there is only a 25% chance of young (2-6 hit dice, 1-4/2-5/2-7/2-8/3-12 hit points damage per attack), numbering 1-4 of the herd. Boars and sows fight equally, and either fights on for 1-4 melee rounds after reaching 0 to −10 hit points, but dies at once at −11 or lower.

Warthog: these tropical animals are aggressive only if their territory is threatened, or if they are cornered or threatened. They make two slashing attacks with their large tusks; males and females fight equally. If 3-6 are met, all but the adults are young (1-2 hit dice, 1-3/2-5 hit points damage per attack). A warthog fights on for 1-2 melee rounds after reaching 0 to −5 hit points, but dies at once at −6 or lower.

A warthog fights on for 1-2 melee rounds after reaching 0 to −5 hit points, but dies at once at −6 or lower.

Small mole-like animals found in most places above and below ground. Brain moles are drawn to psionic activity of any kind, including magic spells that duplicate psionic effects.

  • Burrowing: when within 30’ of any creature using such activity, a brain mole tries to feed on the energy by psionically “burrowing” into the mind. This attacks the user’s mind as a mind thrust of 121 point strength.
  • Non-psionics: a creature without psionic powers that is using psionic energy through spells or magic items has a 20% chance per melee round of being driven permanently insane. Stopping the spell or ceasing to use the item ends the attack at once.
  • Psionics: a psionic under attack must get out of the brain mole’s range or kill it to stop the burrowing.

Brownies are distant relatives of halflings (perhaps half halfling, half pixie), but smaller and far less common. They are basically friendly to humans and their kin (dwarves, elves, and halflings), but shy, so they are seldom seen, and prefer quiet, pastoral places to live.

  • Help: met on friendly terms, brownies can often (50%) be persuaded to help lawful good characters. They easily make or repair items of wood, leather, metal, etc., and are good guides.
  • Spells (once per day each): protection from evil, ventriloquism, dancing lights, continual light, mirror image (3 images), confusion, and dimension door.
  • Abilities: exceptional senses in general; never surprised; 18 dexterity. They can blend into the landscape very quickly, using natural cover and speed to become effectively invisible (and escape, if they wish).
  • Weapons: usually only short swords.
  • Languages: their own and their alignment tongue, plus elvish, pixieish, and the languages of sprites and halflings.

These dangerous herd animals of tropical and subtropical plains usually attack anyone who comes too close (6” or less), and the whole herd is likely to charge.

  • Charge: a charging buffalo does 3-18 hit points of damage on impact and 1-4 points trampling. A charge must cover at least 40’.
  • Some species (50% chance) are not aggressive and flee if threatened.

system.treasure: Individuals J, K, L, M. B in lair
system.description:
Bugbears live in loose bands, usually in the same areas as goblins. Unlike their smaller cousins, these hairy giant goblins work equally well in bright daylight or deep darkness (they have infravision to 60’), so they are as likely to live above ground as below.

  • Leaders: with 12 or more bugbears there is a leader with 22-25 hit points (armor class 4, attacks as a 4 hit dice monster, +1 damage). With 24 or more there are also a chief (armor class 3, 28-30 hit points, attacks as a 4 hit dice monster, +2 damage) and a sub-chief (as the leader).
  • Lair: always a chief and sub-chief, plus females and young each equal to 50% of the number of males. These fight only in a life or death situation: females as hobgoblins, young as kobolds.
  • Weapons: anything available, from swords to spiked wooden clubs (morning stars). Many carry spears, and they tend to throw spears, axes, maces, and hammers as missiles. Being strong, they can throw these up to 4”, with anything under 2” counting as medium range.
  • Stealth: they look clumsy and walk with a shambling gait, but can move very quickly and very quietly, surprising opponents 50% of the time.
  • Languages: goblin and hobgoblin, as well as their own racial and alignment tongues.

Description: skin light yellow to yellow brown, typically dull yellow; hair from lusterless tannish brown to brick red; eyes greenish white with red pupils. The odds and ends of armor they wear, and the cloth, skins, or hides they drape themselves in, are usually ill-kept, dirty, and dingy. They live about 75 years.

The bulette (or landshark) was thought extinct until this horror reappeared recently. It came from a mad wizard’s cross-breeding of a snapping turtle and an armadillo, with infusions of demon ichor. It roams temperate climates, eating horses, men, and most other flesh, though it dislikes dwarf and shuns elf of every kind. It loves halfling and will hungrily dig them out of their burrows. Stupid, irritable, always hungry, and afraid of nothing, a bulette will attack a large, powerful party just to eat a horse or two. Sometimes the crest of a burrowing landshark breaks the ground, which gives it its name.

  • Attacks: it usually uses its front feet and gaping maw. When cornered or badly wounded, it can leap up to 8’ in the air with blinding speed and strike with all four feet (each rear foot also doing 3-18 points of damage).
  • Weak spots: the shell under its crest, an area about a foot and a half square, is only AC 6, and in a fierce fight it tends to raise its crest and expose this area. Its eyes are armor class 4, but small (8” oval).
  • Habits: solitary; only a mated pair shares a territory. No young have ever been seen, though smaller specimens (as few as 6 hit dice) have been killed, and no one knows how or where the young are born or hatched. Very large ones have been reported, one of no less than 11 hit dice and over 11’ tall at the shoulder.
  • Value: the great plates behind its head are highly prized for shields; a skilled dwarven craftsman can make them into a shield of +1 to +3 value.

Description: typically blue-brown head and hindquarters, with plates and scales of gray-blue to blue-green. Nails and teeth are dull ivory. The area around the eyes is brown-black, the eyeballs yellowish, and the pupils dark-green.

The bull is a dangerous opponent, aggressive and easily angered. Wild oxen and aurochs belong to this general class. If approached within 8”, there is a 75% chance it attacks. When a herd is present, several bulls defend the rest.

  • Charge: 3-12 points of damage on impact, plus 1-4 points trampling. A charge must cover at least 30’.

One-humped camels (dromedaries) live only in very warm deserts. Two-humped camels (bactrians) can stand cold and even regions that are not desert. All camels can go up to two weeks without food or water.

  • Loads: up to 6,000 gold pieces of weight, which slows them to 9”. Loaded with 4,000 to 5,000 gold pieces, their speed is 15” at most. The bactrian is 3” slower than the dromedary, so reduce its movement accordingly.
  • Attacks: they bite (they can kick, but usually do not).
  • Temper: they tend to be nasty-tempered and may spit at people who come to ride or use them: a 50% chance of spitting, and if they do, a 25% chance of blinding for 1-3 melee rounds.
  • Horses tend to dislike the smell of camels.

Carrion crawlers look much like a cross between a giant green cutworm and a huge cephalopod, and are usually found only underground. As the name says, it is a scavenger, but it still attacks living creatures aggressively, which keeps it supplied with corpses to eat or to lay its eggs in.

  • Armor: its head is well protected, but its body is only armor class 7.
  • Movement: despite its bulk it moves quite fast on its many legs, and travels walls and ceilings as easily as floors, since each foot has sharp claws that hold it fast.
  • Tentacles: 8 tentacles, each 2’ long, flail at prey from its head. Each oozes a gummy secretion that, when fresh, paralyzes opponents (save versus paralyzation to avoid it). With so many tentacles, and so many chances of paralysis, these monsters are greatly feared.

This nightmare creature is loathsome beyond description and has no redeeming features. Its body is like a huge, bloated buffalo and smells offensive. Its long, thin neck carries a big head uglier than a warthog’s. Its legs are thick and stumpy, like a hippopotamus’s. Perhaps its home, fetid swamps and miasmal marshes, caused this bizarre mix of traits, or perhaps some demented godling tinkered with life. Either way, the most horrible thing about it is its bloodshot eyes.

  • Tail: strong and snaky, it strikes enemies with amazing speed. A creature struck has a base 75% chance of being stunned for 1-10 melee rounds, reduced by 5% for every level (or hit die for monsters) above 1. So an 11th-level character struck by the tail has only a 25% chance of being stunned.
  • Gaze: equal to a death ray, reaching 6” from the eyes (even into the astral and ethereal planes). Any creature meeting it dies with no chance to save.
  • Raising the head: on complete surprise (a 2 on d6), one of the party has met its gaze. Otherwise its very weak neck has only a 25% chance of raising the head high enough to use its eyes; if both sides stay still, this chance rises by 15% per melee round. If it must follow quick movements, or is shambling after prey, the chance is only 10% per melee round.
  • Fleeing: a fleeing victim, even with eyes averted, is still subject to the deadly gaze, but gets a saving throw.

Wild cattle roam many wilderness areas and are often met. They are likely to flee any threat.

  • Bulls: if intruders come upon the herd before it can run away, the males are likely (75%) to attack (see BULL).
  • Stampede: there is also a 25% chance the herd stampedes straight at the party. If there is no cover (rocks, trees, logs, a wall, etc.), roll 2d4 for each party member in its path to find how many cattle trample him or her. Each trampling animal does 1-4 hit points of damage.

system.treasure: M, Q, with each; D, I, T in lair
system.description:
Centaurs live in secluded pastures far from human settlements. Roving bands always carry weapons, and leaders carry shields.

  • Arms of a band: half carry oaken clubs (equal to morning stars, 1-8 or 1-6 hit points damage per attack); one-quarter carry composite long bows and 10-30 arrows (24” range, 1-6 hit points damage per attack); the remaining quarter are leaders (AC 4) with shield and lance (1-8 or 2-24 hit points damage per attack). Leaders have double treasure.
  • Melee: each centaur attacks twice: once with his weapon, then as a horse with his two front hooves.
  • Lair: a hidden glen with rich grass and running water, holding 1-6 more males, twice as many females as males, and 5-30 young. Females (3 hit dice) and young (1-3 hit dice) use no weapons and fight with their hooves only in a life and death situation. If the females and young are threatened, the centaurs are 90% likely to ransom them with their main treasure.
  • Languages: their own and their alignment tongue.
  • Relations: not generally friendly with humans or dwarves; they tolerate gnomes and halflings, are friendly with elves, and like wood elves.

These nasty creatures are found nearly everywhere, in many colors from pale gray to black and red to brown. They are aggressive and rush out to bite their prey, injecting poison into the wound.

  • Poison: often weak and not fatal (+4 on the saving throw roll).
  • Small size: it resists attacks that allow it a saving throw less well (−1 on the die).

system.specialDefenses: Not harmed except by cure disease
system.description:
These creatures are invisible to the human eye. They can be detected only psionically, by carefully examining a person’s aura, and removed only by a cure disease spell. They live on the astral and ethereal planes as well as the material plane, and cannot be attacked psionically.

  • Infestation: if a psionic creature comes within 1” of cerebral parasites, they attack it, completely unnoticed.
  • Feeding: from then on, whenever psionic abilities (including attacks and defenses) are used, each parasite drains one extra psionic energy point to feed on.
  • Breeding: after a parasite has fed on six psionic energy points, it produces another parasite, and both keep draining energy, as will its offspring.
system.hpNote: Hit dice not applicable (MM p.14); it is removed only by cure disease.

system.description:
The chimera monstrously combines three creatures: the hindquarters of a huge goat, the forequarters of a lion, dragon wings, and three large heads.

  • Attacks: it claws with its forelegs; the goat head has two long horns; the lion head has powerful jaws and sharp teeth, as does the dragon head.
  • Breath: if it wishes (50% chance), the dragon head breathes fire to a range of 5”, doing 3-24 points of damage (saving throw applies).
  • Language: a very limited form of the red dragon language.

Description: the goat parts are black, with amber eyes and yellowish horns. The lion parts are tawny yellow with a dark brown mane, green eyes, and a red maw. The dragon wings are brownish-black, the dragon head orange, and its eyes and mouth black.

Cockatrices live in temperate to tropical regions, above and below ground. Their beaks do only minor wounds, but their touch turns flesh to stone (save versus stone or be petrified). Their petrifying aura extends into the astral and ethereal planes and can affect creatures there too (compare BASILISK).

Description: a yellow-green serpent’s tail, yellow feet and beak, gray wings, golden brown feathers, and red wattles, comb, eyes, and tongue.

These winged, feathered serpents are rarely found anywhere but warm, jungle-like regions, or flying through the ether. Their intelligence and powers make the people of their homelands regard them with awe as divine. Couatl rarely interfere in human affairs.

  • Powers: they can polymorph themselves, and use magic as a 5th-level magic-user and/or 7th-level cleric (45% use magic-user spells, 35% cleric spells, 20% both).
  • Melee: a poisonous bite (saving throw applies) and constriction. A successful constriction does 2-8 hit points of damage that melee round and every round after, until one or the other is killed.
  • Psionics: 2 major and 4 minor disciplines, with matching attack and defense modes.
  • Languages: several human languages and most serpent and bird languages.

Giant crabs live near water of any kind. They are equally at home on land or in water and are always looking for something to eat. Their stalked eyes can easily peek over ledges or around corners. They tend to hide and rush out to seize their prey (surprising on 1-4 on d6).
These strange monsters live only in fresh water. They walk slowly but can swim very fast for short periods. Like giant crabs, they hide and rush out to seize their prey (surprising on 1-3 on d6).

Some of these reptiles are giant-sized, but those are usually found only in salt water or prehistoric settings. All crocodiles are stupid and voracious. They are sluggish in cold weather (movement cut by 50%). They usually lie hidden to surprise prey (surprising on 1-3 on d6).

Some of these reptiles are giant-sized, but those are usually found only in salt water or prehistoric settings. All crocodiles are stupid and voracious. They are sluggish in cold weather (movement cut by 50%). They usually lie hidden to surprise prey (surprising on 1-3 on d6).

Rivalry between demon lords is great, but the enmity between Demogorgon and Orcus is immense and never-ending. Demogorgon is a terrible opponent.

His heads:

  • Both heads together: when he fixes both gazes on his enemies, he can hypnotize 10-100 creatures of 1 to 3 hit dice, 5 to 40 of 4 to 6 hit dice, 3 to 24 of 7 to 9 hit dice, 2 to 12 of 10 to 12 hit dice, or 1-4 of 13 or more hit dice. Those over 15 hit dice save versus magic; all others are hypnotized automatically. This mass hypnosis lasts only 1 turn, but during it victims follow most instructions absolutely (they will not destroy themselves), and for 1 to 6 turns afterward they tend to believe or carry out what remains of it.
  • Each head alone: the left head’s gaze works as a rod of beguiling; the right head’s causes insanity for 1 to 6 turns. Used separately like this, potential victims save versus magic to avoid the eyes.

Tail: he lashes his forked tail like a whip. It hits as a flail, and its touch drains one to four energy levels.

Tentacles: each does 1-6 hit points of damage. Lesser opponents (especially those from the material plane, such as humans, dwarves, and elves) also suffer rot: a limb hit becomes useless in 6 melee rounds and drops off after another six; a body hit permanently removes 25% of the victim’s hit points in 6 melee rounds, cumulative per hit. A cure disease within those 6 melee rounds saves a limb, which then heals in 1 to 4 weeks, and fully restores body hits.

Powers (any one at a time, whenever he wishes): continual darkness, charm person, create illusion (as an illusion wand), cause fear (as a fear wand), levitate (as a 16th-level magic-user), detect magic, read magic, read languages, detect invisible objects, ESP, dispel magic, clairvoyance, clairaudience, suggestion, water breathing, polymorph self, wall of ice, charm monster, telekinesis of 7,000 gold piece weight with each of his two heads (or with just one), project image, sticks to snakes, and gate in other demons (85% chance of success: 50% a type I-IV, 50% a type V or VI). Once per day each: feeblemind, power word stun, and any symbol.

Description: some claim this demon prince is supreme; in any case his power is awesome. He is a gigantic reptilian demon 18’ tall. His two heads have the faces of evil baboons, or perhaps mandrills with their hideous coloring. His blue-green skin is plated with snake-like scales, his body and legs are a giant lizard’s, his twin necks are like snakes, and his thick tail is forked. Instead of arms he has great tentacles. His look shows his command of cold-blooded things such as serpents, reptiles, and octopi.

Demons: general (MM)

Each type of demon, and especially the high-level demon lords and princes, has many unusual traits and extraordinary abilities. This section covers what all demons share; see each demon for its own details.

  • Planes: demons can move from their own plane to Tarterus, Hades, or Pandemonium, or roam the astral plane. They cannot enter the material plane without help (conjuration, a gate, speaking their name, or similar means). They often roam the astral and ethereal planes, and persons in an ethereal state attract their attention.
  • Nature: chaotic and evil. The smarter and stronger rule the weaker and less intelligent. The less intelligent attack without question and fight until slain.
  • Death: demons of type V and above are not truly slain when their material form is killed in combat. They lose that form and are forced back to their own plane, where they must stay until a century has passed or someone helps them come forth again. Demons met on their own plane can be slain.
  • Other traits: no demon can ever be subdued. All can split their attacks between two or even three opponents if their means allow.
  • Service: demons never willingly serve anyone or anything. Forced to serve by magic or threat, they constantly look for a way to kill their master or captor. Those they take a liking to are usually carried off to their plane as slaves (though favored ones). Characters of any alignment can summon demons, but controlling one is another matter entirely. A thaumaturgic circle keeps out demons of types I-V; types VI and greater need a special pentacle. The DM must handle carefully any threat or reward used to try to gain a demon’s service. Holy (good) relics or artifacts repel demons.

Demons’ amulets: demon lords and princes keep their vital essence (their souls, so to speak) in small containers, which protects them but leaves them vulnerable if an enterprising character gets the amulet.

  • A demon with its amulet can magic jar once per day.
  • No magic can detect an amulet as such, and it looks ordinary in every way. The most powerful princes need not keep theirs with them, but lesser demons usually carry theirs on or near them.
  • Holding a demon’s amulet gives power over that demon for, for example, one adventure, and never more than a day (24 hours). Then the amulet must be returned to the demon, or it can be destroyed, which condemns the prince to the abyss for a year (and he can return after that only if summoned).
  • Using one is very, very dangerous. Holding one doubles the chance of drawing another demon’s attention, and any demon not controlled by it attacks the holder at once. If the amulet leaves the hand of the person commanding its demon, that demon at once attacks him in its most effective way, trying its utmost to slay him and carry all that remains to its own domain: that character is lost forever.
  • On the other hand, if the holder carefully repays the demon for its help, adds a considerable sum for daring to command it in the first place, and then carefully returns the amulet, the prince might not hold a grudge forever or hunt him whenever possible.

Speaking a name: if the name of a particularly powerful demon is spoken, he may hear and turn his attention to the speaker; a base 5% chance is suggested. Unless the speaker is prepared to avoid this attention, or to control the demon, the demon at once kills the speaker by the quickest means.

In the lair: demons of types I through VI found in their lair are 1-6 of the same type 75% of the time, and 1-6 of mixed types I-VI 25% of the time.

Weapons: types I-III are affected by non-magical weapons; type IV and greater are not.

All demons have these abilities:

InfravisionTeleportation (no error)
Darkness (r. varies)Gate (specifics vary)

Attack forms: demons take damage from these as shown:

AttackMaximum Damage Will be:
acidfull
coldhalf
electricity (lightning)half
fire (dragon, magical)half
gas (poisonous, etc.)half
iron weaponfull
magic missilefull
poisonfull
silver weaponnone*

* Unless the demon is affected by normal weapons, in which case damage is by weapon type.

Telepathy: a special form of telepathy lets demons understand every intelligent communication, and those of average or better intelligence can also converse.

Without question the most disgusting and loathsome of all demons, foul and nauseating in the extreme. Juiblex is reclusive and hates intrusion by any normal creature, and other demons and creatures likewise shun him. He surrounds himself with slimes, jellies, and puddings: in his lair there are 1-4 green slimes, 2-8 ochre jellies, 1-4 gray oozes, and 1-4 black puddings.

  • Melee: his dripping form lashes out to do terrible damage, both from the force of the blow and from his caustic, noisome secretions.
  • At will: a circle of darkness (15’ radius). He can also cause fear (as a fear wand), cast a circle of cold (10’ radius), and regenerate 2 hit points per melee round.
  • One per melee round: detect invisible, locate object, ESP, fly, dispel magic, invisibility (10’ radius), charm monster, hold monster, telekinesis of 15,000 gold piece weight, project image, phase door, putrefy food & water, cause disease, speak with monsters, an unholy word (once per day), and gate in 1-4 type II demons (70% chance of success).
  • Slime: once per turn (every ten melee rounds) he can spew a jelly-like slime combining the effects of an ochre jelly and green slime, with a 15’ range and a blob 3 cubic feet in size.

Description: Juiblex has no fixed form. He can spread into a vast pool of slime or rise into a towering column of disgusting filth 18’ or more high, but usually takes the form of a cone-shaped heap 9’ tall, streaked with disgusting blackish greens, foul browns and yellows, and sickly translucent grays and ambers. Several glaring red eyes stick out of the mass.

acidfull

electricity (lightning)half
fire (dragon, magical)half
gas (poisonous, etc.)half
iron weaponfull
magic missilefull
poisonfull
silver weaponnone*

The dead who go to the 666 layers of the demonic abyss become manes; the most evil of them are confined in the tiers of flame of Gehenna. They are only semi-intelligent and attack any non-demon with nails and teeth.

  • Death: killing one only dissipates it into a stinking cloud of vapor that re-forms as manes in one day. Demon lords and princes sometimes feed on them, destroying them utterly.
  • Spells: treat them as undead against sleep, charm, and similar spells.
  • Uses: certain manes are made into shadows or ghasts, depending on how great their evil was in material life. A lord or prince can also send them to the material plane for a day; these usually come from Gehenna.

This creature is probably one of the most powerful and strongest of all demons.

  • Melee: even a slap with his open hand does 1-4 hit points of damage; his terrible fists do 3-13. With a weapon he gets +6 to hit and +8 on damage.
  • Tail: it strikes with 18 dexterity, doing 2-8 hit points per hit, and carries a virulent poison sting (−4 on all saving throws against it).
  • Powers (any one at will): continual darkness, charm person, create illusion (as an illusion wand), cause fear (as a fear wand), detect magic, read magic, read languages, detect invisible objects, ESP, pyrotechnics, dispel magic, clairvoyance, clairaudience, a 12-die lightning bolt, suggestion, polymorph self, wall of fire, telekinesis of 12,000 gold piece weight, animate dead (as a 19th-level magic-user), project image, polymorph any object, and shape change. Once per day: feeblemind, time stop, and each of the symbols. He can speak with dead (as a 20th-level cleric).
  • Gating: an 80% chance of gating in any demon of type I-V (but only a 50% chance for a type V or VI); he never calls another prince.
  • Undead: as their prince, he can summon certain undead. For a random call, roll d4: 1, 4-48 skeletons; 2, 4-32 zombies; 3, 4-24 shadows; 4, 2-8 vampires.

By merely touching their flesh it causes death (or annihilation) to any creature except those of equal status (other princes or devils, saints, godlings, etc.). Its other powers, as rumored among mortals, are covered in another book.

Description: a grossly fat demon lord some 15’ tall. His huge gray body is covered in goatish hair, and his head is goat-like but with a ram’s horns. His great legs are also goat-like, but his arms are human. Vast bat wings sprout from his back, and his long, snaky tail ends in a poisonous head.

Demons: general (MM)

Each type of demon, and especially the high-level demon lords and princes, has many unusual traits and extraordinary abilities. This section covers what all demons share; see each demon for its own details.

  • Planes: demons can move from their own plane to Tarterus, Hades, or Pandemonium, or roam the astral plane. They cannot enter the material plane without help (conjuration, a gate, speaking their name, or similar means). They often roam the astral and ethereal planes, and persons in an ethereal state attract their attention.
  • Nature: chaotic and evil. The smarter and stronger rule the weaker and less intelligent. The less intelligent attack without question and fight until slain.
  • Death: demons of type V and above are not truly slain when their material form is killed in combat. They lose that form and are forced back to their own plane, where they must stay until a century has passed or someone helps them come forth again. Demons met on their own plane can be slain.
  • Other traits: no demon can ever be subdued. All can split their attacks between two or even three opponents if their means allow.
  • Service: demons never willingly serve anyone or anything. Forced to serve by magic or threat, they constantly look for a way to kill their master or captor. Those they take a liking to are usually carried off to their plane as slaves (though favored ones). Characters of any alignment can summon demons, but controlling one is another matter entirely. A thaumaturgic circle keeps out demons of types I-V; types VI and greater need a special pentacle. The DM must handle carefully any threat or reward used to try to gain a demon’s service. Holy (good) relics or artifacts repel demons.

Demons’ amulets: demon lords and princes keep their vital essence (their souls, so to speak) in small containers, which protects them but leaves them vulnerable if an enterprising character gets the amulet.

  • A demon with its amulet can magic jar once per day.
  • No magic can detect an amulet as such, and it looks ordinary in every way. The most powerful princes need not keep theirs with them, but lesser demons usually carry theirs on or near them.
  • Holding a demon’s amulet gives power over that demon for, for example, one adventure, and never more than a day (24 hours). Then the amulet must be returned to the demon, or it can be destroyed, which condemns the prince to the abyss for a year (and he can return after that only if summoned).
  • Using one is very, very dangerous. Holding one doubles the chance of drawing another demon’s attention, and any demon not controlled by it attacks the holder at once. If the amulet leaves the hand of the person commanding its demon, that demon at once attacks him in its most effective way, trying its utmost to slay him and carry all that remains to its own domain: that character is lost forever.
  • On the other hand, if the holder carefully repays the demon for its help, adds a considerable sum for daring to command it in the first place, and then carefully returns the amulet, the prince might not hold a grudge forever or hunt him whenever possible.

Speaking a name: if the name of a particularly powerful demon is spoken, he may hear and turn his attention to the speaker; a base 5% chance is suggested. Unless the speaker is prepared to avoid this attention, or to control the demon, the demon at once kills the speaker by the quickest means.

Each type VI demon has its own name; six are known to exist. (Balor is a type VI demon of the largest size.)

  • Weapons: a large +1 sword and a whip with many “tails”, used to drag opponents into the flames these demons can create around themselves.
  • Flames: in combat there is a two-thirds chance (1-4 on d6) each melee round that a type VI demon bursts into flame and uses its whip. A victim drawn into the flames takes 4-24 hit points of damage from the two largest, 3-18 from the middle-sized, and 2-12 from the smallest.
  • Darkness: 10’ radius at will.
  • Other abilities (as often as desired, but only one at a time): cause fear (as a fear wand), detect magic, read magic, read languages, detect invisible objects, pyrotechnics, dispel magic, suggestion, telekinesis of 6,000 gold piece weight, a symbol of fear, discord, sleep, or stunning, and a 70% chance of gating in a demon of type III (80%) or type IV (20%).

With the proper invocation, offerings, and promises, a type VI demon might be persuaded to cooperate with a character or group for a while, though it will naturally try to take over command at every chance. Most chaotic evil monsters are drawn to its strong evil charisma. Of all demons, type VI leans toward a more organized evil, which makes it unpopular with demon lords and princes.

Among the demon princes, Yeenoghu is one of the most powerful and most feared.

  • Followers: normally 66 of the strongest gnolls (14-16 hit points each) attend him. Alone, he can summon 6-66 gnolls in one turn. Because the King of Ghouls also pays him homage, he can summon 6-16 ghouls if he wishes.
  • Flail: he usually carries his dreaded flail, 7’ long, with three adamantite chains each ending in a spiked ball. Roll to hit separately for each ball: the 1st does 3 to 18 points of damage; the 2nd, if it hits, paralyzes unless the victim saves versus wands; the 3rd, if it hits, confuses (as the spell) unless the victim saves versus magic.
  • Speech: he speaks all the “giant class” languages and the common tongue. He can telepathically project his speech to any single creature, but cannot influence it that way beyond the persuasiveness of his words.
  • Senses: he sees into the ethereal and astral planes.
  • One per melee round: darkness (10’ radius); magic missile (3 per day, 6 missiles per casting, each doing 2-8 points of damage at +2 to hit); detect magic, read magic, read languages, detect invisible objects, invisibility, fly, hold person, dispel magic (as a 20th-level magic-user), suggestion, polymorph self, fear (as a fear wand), teleport, telekinesis of 10,000 gold piece weight, transmute rock to mud, mass charm, and gate in type I demons (once per day, 80% chance, 2-5 of them).

Description: at first glance he looks like a human in general shape, but his head is a hyena’s, his chest is canine, and his hands and feet are paws. He is thin to the point of being skeletal, and his only body hair is a mangy crest of putrid yellow running from his head to the middle of his back. His smooth skin is dead gray, and his large eyes are glowing amber.

Asmodeus, the arch-fiend, overlord of all the dukes of Hell, rules by both might and wit. He is physically stronger than any other devil (as strong as a storm giant) and the most cunning and artful. His mighty palace stands on the floor of the lowest rift in Hell’s ninth plane. His servants are pit fiends and whatever other lesser and greater devils he commands. Once per year he can summon the arch-devils to attend his court and pay homage.

  • At will (once per turn or melee round): pyrotechnics, produce flame, wall of fire, ice storm, wall of ice, continual light, read languages, read magic, detect invisible, locate object, invisibility, dispel magic, hold person, hold monster, shape change, beguile, rulership, mass charm, geas, restoration, raise dead fully, or (fulfill another’s) wish.
  • Once per day: symbol of pain, symbol of insanity, symbol of hopelessness (save versus magic or submit to his will), and (un)holy word.
  • Summoning: he can always summon 2 lesser devils or 1 greater devil.
  • Gaze: at his choice it causes fear, fear and weakness, or chill (slowed 50% and −5 on all dice rolls). Saving throw versus magic applies.
  • Ruby rod: he carries a glowing rod of pure ruby that works as a rod of absorption and causes serious wounds to anyone touched by its opaline tip. On command it shoots a cone of frost, a jet of acid, or a bolt of lightning (each as the matching dragon breath weapon). Its gem value alone is 1,000,000 gold pieces.

Description: without question the most handsome of all devils, as well as the strongest and most cunning. The ultimate evil he represents shows in his beauty only when he wishes it, or when he forgets himself and flies into a rage.

Devils: general (MM)

The inhabitants and rulers of the planes of Hell are mainly devils, the most powerful of lawful evil creatures. They are somewhat like the demons of chaos in their traits and abilities. This section covers what they share; each type and arch-devil has its own entry.

  • Order: devils follow a definite chain of command, which they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Still, there is great rivalry, even open hostility, between the devils of the different planes and between the arch-devils. While lesser devils squabble, the dukes of Hell compete to seize Asmodeus’ throne, but the Archfiend has always played one against another and still rules from his lowest plane.
  • Planes: all devils can move about the planes of Hell (though, except for the dukes, they dare not without authorization), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can travel the astral plane but seldom do. No devil can enter any other plane unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or a devil’s proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke of Hell can be destroyed, but such creatures cannot truly be slain unless met and fought in Hell or the lower planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is forced into lemure form for nine decades of torment before it regains its former rank. A duke whose material form is destroyed is bound to its own plane of Hell for a decade (unless properly called forth again before the 10 years are up) and suffers a great loss of face (and Hell’s fury is then unmatched).
  • Fighting: devils can never be subdued. Lesser devils always fight until destroyed; greater ones negotiate if seriously threatened. All devils can split their attacks between two or more opponents if they have the means.
  • Service: devils will serve if properly commanded, but it is risky: an improper command breaks the law binding them to service. (Usually a contract for the soul of whoever commands them is also needed.) Persons other than lawful evil ones can invoke or deal with devils, but had better use the proverbial long spoon when supping with them. Properly drawn magic circles keep devils off for a time (with symbols added for greater devils and arch-devils). Holy (good) artifacts or relics repel devils.

Devils’ talismans: each type of lesser devil has a special combination of inscriptions that binds those devils to the wielder for nine days, or at least keeps devils of that type from harming the holder. Greater devils can likewise be commanded for nine hours or kept at bay. Properly used, an arch-devil’s talisman makes it perform a single service, or keeps a particular duke of Hell from harming the bearer.

  • Using any devil’s talisman needs great care and caution, and evil creatures must make a human sacrifice to use one.
  • Even looking at one is dangerous. Studying one without protection by spells or a magic circle gives a 10% chance of summoning the kind of devil, or the particular devil, it belongs to. Speaking the name on it always calls that devil forth.
  • Arch-devils know of improperly protected talismans, and send something to slay whoever holds one that concerns them or their planes.

General characteristics:

  • Weapons: only erinyes, barbed devils, and bone devils can be hit by non-magical weapons. The greater devils (malebranche, ice devils, and pit fiends) can be struck by magical or silver weapons, but ordinary arms do them no harm.
  • Abilities of all devils: charm person, suggestion, illusion, infravision, teleportation (no error), know alignment, cause fear (effect varies), and animate dead.
  • Summoning: devils can summon their fellows, much like a monster summoning spell.
  • Telepathy: a special form of telepathy lets them understand and talk with any intelligent creature.

Baalzebul, “Lord of the Flies” (“lies”?), rules the sixth and seventh planes of Hell, Malbolge and Maladomini. He is an arch-devil of great power, second only to Asmodeus. Malbolge is a plane of black stone, full of stinking vapors, smoke, fire pits, and huge caves and caverns. Maladomini is similar, but holds the moated castles of the malebranche and Baalzebul’s great fortress.

  • At will (one at a time, per turn or melee round): pyrotechnics, produce flame, wall of fire, continual light, read languages, read magic, detect invisible, locate object, invisibility, dispel magic, shape change, beguile, rulership (as a rod of rulership), hold person, charm monster, geas, restoration, raise dead fully, or (fulfill another’s) wish.
  • Once per day: symbol of pain, symbol of insanity, and (un)holy word.
  • Summoning: he can always summon 1-4 horned devils.
  • Glance: whenever he stares straight at someone, it causes fear and weakness (save versus magic or collapse, trembling, until 1-4 melee rounds after his gaze moves away).

Barbed devils live on the third and fourth planes of Hell. They are excellent guards, always alert (never surprised). Unauthorized creatures are thrown at once into one of the many cells to be tormented.

  • One at a time (per turn or melee round): pyrotechnics, produce flame, hold person, or summon another barbed devil (30% chance of success).

Dispater rules Hell’s second plane. His capital is the iron city of Dis, named after the whole plane, and his palace there is infernally grand. The city is full of zombies, erinyes, and a sprinkling of barbed devils and malebranche.

  • At will (one at a time, per turn or melee round): pyrotechnics, produce flame, wall of fire, light, read magic, read languages, detect invisible, shape change, beguile, geas, restoration, raise dead fully, or (fulfill another’s) wish.
  • Summoning: 1-3 erinyes (75%) or a pit fiend (25%), with a 90% chance of success.
  • Once per day: a symbol of pain, and an (un)holy word.
  • Stare: causes fear or chill in everyone who fails a saving throw versus magic.

Description: evilly handsome; only his small horns, tail, and cloven left hoof set him apart from humanity. He carries a rod with the powers of a rod of rulership and a double strength staff of striking (4-24 hit points of damage).

The erinyes are the common devils of Hell’s second plane, and the kind most often sent out to gather more souls. They are female but can appear male. They relentlessly pursue evil persons to take them alive into Hell, and sometimes bargain with others, hoping to tempt them into evil.

  • Weapons: a magical dagger dripping caustic venom that causes terribly painful wounds (save versus poison or faint for 1-6 melee rounds), and a rope of entanglement to bind their victims.
  • Defenses: normal weapons can strike them.
  • Fear: at will, everyone who looks at them is affected by cause fear (saving throw versus wand applies).
  • One per turn or melee round: detect invisible, locate object, invisibility, polymorph self, produce flame, or summon another erinyes (25% chance of success).
  • Strength: 18/01, but with no hit or damage bonuses.

Sometimes called the “Wild Beast”, Geryon is the gigantic ruler of the fifth plane of Hell, as powerful as a storm giant. He lives in a huge castle in the very middle of the plane and seldom goes out.

  • Melee: he loves to grab opponents and rend them with his claws while stabbing them with his terrible poisonous tail (save versus poison at −4 on the die).
  • At will (once per melee round or turn): ice storm, wall of ice, light, read languages, read magic, detect invisible, locate object, dispel magic, invisibility, shape change, beguile, geas, raise dead fully, or (fulfill another’s) wish.
  • Once per day: a symbol of pain, and an (un)holy word.
  • Summoning: 1-2 bone devils (60%) or an ice devil (40%), with a 95% chance of success.
  • Glare: causes fear in everyone he directs it at (saving throw versus magic applies).
  • Horn: he has a great bull’s horn that, when blown, brings 5-20 minotaurs who obey him to the death. It can be blown only once per week.

Description: a handsome head and torso on a snake-like body. He has no legs and moves along the ground like a snake. He has huge bat wings and a barbed tail dripping poison. His arms are strong and hairy, ending in paw-like hands.

The “evil horns” (male branche) come mainly from Hell’s sixth and seventh planes. They are the least of the greater devils, with names such as “Dogretch”, “Evil Tail”, and “Bent Wing”. They hate anything stronger than themselves, and fear stronger devils accordingly.

  • Weapons: if armed, a two-tined fork (75%) doing 2-12 points of damage, or a barbed whip (25%) doing 1-4 points plus stunning for the same number of melee rounds unless the victim saves versus magic. Unarmed, they attack with claw/claw/bite.
  • Tail: armed or not, they can also strike with their tails for 1-3 hit points, leaving a wound that keeps bleeding until bound (1 hit point lost per turn until bound or cured).
  • Fear: they exude fear in a 5’ radius (saving throw versus wand applies).
  • At will (once per turn or melee round): pyrotechnics, produce flame, ESP, detect magic, illusion, or summon another horned devil (50% chance of success).
  • Once per day: a wall of fire of triple normal strength for damage (3-24 hit points).

  • Other traits: ultravision (60’), regenerate 1 hit point per melee round, and a grasping strength of 18/76. They radiate fear in a 10’ radius (saving throw vs. wand applies).

Lemures are the form given to the dead who dwell in the Nine Hells: vaguely human blobs that the devils torment. Their minds are quite gone, and they attack anything non-devilish they see. After some time in Hell, certain lemures are chosen to become wraiths or spectres.

  • Regeneration: 1 hit point per melee round, so the wounds dealt by their surroundings or by the devils seldom destroy them.
  • Destruction: only blessed things (holy water, holy swords, etc.) destroy them permanently.
  • They are immune to all forms of sleep, charm, and the like.

  • Even looking at one is dangerous. Studying one without protection by spells or a magic circle gives a 10% chance of summoning the kind of devil, or the particular devil, it belongs to. Speaking the name on it always calls that devil forth.

General characteristics:

  • Weapons: only erinyes, barbed devils, and bone devils can be hit by non-magical weapons. The greater devils (malebranche, ice devils, and pit fiends) can be struck by magical or silver weapons, but ordinary arms do them no harm.

Plant-eating, duck-billed dinosaurs. They run from attack; their only defense is a lashing tail.

Dinosaurs: general (MM)

Dinosaurs (the name comes from the Greek for “terrible lizard”) are reptiles descended from creatures called thecodonts. There are two orders: saurischians, which include all the meat-eating dinosaurs, and ornithischians, which include all the armored and/or horned ones.

Because time works strangely on planes where magic works, dinosaurs from widely separated eras are covered together here; they may be found mixed together on some alternate world, strange plane, or isolated continent. No one kind is given great detail, but all the major forms are shown.

  • Nature: all are extremely stupid and driven mainly by hunger. The predators are ferocious and voracious. The plant-eaters are also insatiable, but tend either to ignore anything inedible that does not seem to threaten them, or to flee in panic from anything they see as dangerous. Some plant-eaters defend themselves aggressively and are dangerous, notably stegosaurs, ankylosaurs, and ceratopsians.
  • Marine dinosaurs may overturn vessels to get at the “food” on board, or snatch unsuspecting creatures from the decks of passing ships.
  • Land meat-eaters chase anything that looks or smells edible, stopping only when the prey has clearly got completely out of reach.
  • Plant-eating herds may stampede in almost any direction, as long as it is away from one of the big meat-eaters. Any creature directly in the path is carried along or killed (killed if it is smaller, slower, and weaker).

The plant-eaters are also insatiable, but tend either to ignore anything inedible that does not seem to threaten them, or to flee in panic from anything they see as dangerous. Some plant-eaters defend themselves aggressively and are dangerous, notably stegosaurs, ankylosaurs, and ceratopsians.
  • Marine dinosaurs may overturn vessels to get at the “food” on board, or snatch unsuspecting creatures from the decks of passing ships.
  • Land meat-eaters chase anything that looks or smells edible, stopping only when the prey has clearly got completely out of reach.
  • Plant-eating herds may stampede in almost any direction, as long as it is away from one of the big meat-eaters. Any creature directly in the path is carried along or killed (killed if it is smaller, slower, and weaker).

These reptiles look somewhat like a single-horned rhinoceros. A bone shield protects the head and neck (armor class 3), and the skin is very thick, almost plated. They eat plants but tend to be somewhat aggressive. Charging, they trample smaller creatures for 2-16 hit points of damage.

system.description:
A pack of these monsters contains only full-grown beasts. They hate all life, but blink dogs most of all.

  • Displacement: its molecular vibrations make it always appear 3’ away (left, right, ahead, or behind) from where it really is. So opponents always subtract 2 from their attack rolls against it, and add 2 to their saving throw rolls against it.
  • Attacks: it lashes out with its two tentacles, whose rough, horny edges cause horrible wounds.

Description: vaguely puma-like and bluish black. Its tentacles are dead black with brownish yellow horny edges, and its eyes glow a hellish green.

The djinn come from the aerial (elemental air) plane. They can travel the elemental planes, the astral plane, and the material plane. Their society is ruled by a Caliph served by various nobles and officials (vizers, beys, emirs, sheiks, sherrifs, and maliks).

Once per day each, a djinni can:

  • create nutritious food for 2-12 persons;
  • create water or wine for 2-12 persons;
  • create soft goods or wooden items, permanently (up to about 16 cubic feet of soft goods or 9 cubic feet of wood);
  • create short-lived metal items of up to about 1,000 gold pieces weight (the harder the metal, the shorter it lasts: gold lasts about 24 hours, djinni steel only 1 hour);
  • create an illusion with sight and sound that lasts without concentration until magically dispelled or touched;
  • become invisible, assume gaseous form, wind walk, or form a whirlwind.

Whirlwind: cone-shaped, 1” across at the base, 3” across at the top, and up to 7” high (as the djinni wishes). It takes one full turn to form and one full turn to dissolve, and lasts 1 melee round. It does 2-12 hit points of damage to any non-aerial creature it meets, and sweeps away and kills all creatures of under two hit dice that it meets.

Air creatures: against attacks by creatures based on the element of air, djinn take −1 on damage, and those attackers’ “to hit” rolls are also at −1.

Carrying: a djinni can carry up to 6,000 gold pieces weight, walking or flying, without tiring. It can carry double that for a short time: three turns walking, but only one turn aloft. Each 1,000 gold piece weight under that maximum adds one turn to walking or flying time. Afterward it must rest for six turns.

Masters: capturing and enslaving djinn is best left to the referee. Note that a good master usually encourages a djinni to greater effort and better performance, while a demanding, cruel master gets the opposite.

Noble djinni (1% chance): can grant its master three wishes, but does no other service, and is freed from servitude when it grants the third. Noble djinn are as strong as efreet, have 10 hit dice, strike for 3-24 points of damage, and their whirlwind does 3-18 hit points of damage.

Languages: their own tongue, and, through a limited telepathy that lets them speak appropriately, that of any intelligent person or beast they meet.

War dog: simply large dogs trained to fight, loyal to their masters and ferocious in attack. They usually wear light studded leather armor and a spiked collar. How many appear depends on their masters.

Wild dog: packs of wild dogs live in most regions, sometimes in ranges overlapping those of wolves. When well fed, they simply avoid contact. They can be tamed only if separated from the pack.

War dog: simply large dogs trained to fight, loyal to their masters and ferocious in attack. They usually wear light studded leather armor and a spiked collar. How many appear depends on their masters.

Wild dog: packs of wild dogs live in most regions, sometimes in ranges overlapping those of wolves. When well fed, they simply avoid contact. They can be tamed only if separated from the pack.

Most dolphins simply roam the oceans in nomadic schools, but a small number (10%) have formed underwater communities. If one community is found, there is a 75% chance of 1-4 more within a 5 mile radius. Communal dolphins have guards, depending on the climate: 2-5 swordfish (AC 6, move 24”, 1 + 1 hit dice, 2-12 hit points damage per attack) or 1-3 narwhales (AC 6, move 21”, 4 + 4 hit dice, 2-24 hit points damage per attack).

Dolphins attack any creature that threatens them, and they help humans in distress. They especially hate sharks of all kinds, and attack them unless outnumbered by 2 or more to 1.

These two-legged creatures can change their shape to look like any humanoid creature from 4’ to 8’ tall that they observe, including the creature’s clothing and equipment as well as its body. Having become someone’s double, a doppleganger tries to do away with the victim and take its place. If it cannot, it simply attacks, counting on the confusion to make it impossible to tell it from the creature it copies (surprise means this works).

  • Abilities: ESP, and imitation with 90% accuracy.
  • Defenses: immune to sleep and charm spells. Although it has only 4 hit dice, it makes all saving throws as a 10th-level fighter.

Chance of: speaking 30%; magic use 10%; sleeping 50%.

Black dragons are usually found in miasmal swamps or marshes, but they also live underground, since they always try to lair in deep, dark caves. In their evil they lean toward the midpoint between law and chaos.

  • Attacks: claw/claw/bite, or breath.
  • Breath: it spits acid in a stream ½” wide that extends 6” in a straight line, starting at the height of the dragon’s head and going in the direction and at the angle its head was facing.
  • Spells: a black dragon that speaks and uses magic has one 1st-level spell for each stage of its maturity (1-8 spells). Roll randomly for which it knows; repeats are possible if the rolls say so. They are a special form of the normal spells needing only a spoken component, and each can be used only once per day.

Dragons: general (MM)

Dragons come in many colors, sizes, shapes, and alignments. Two (the Chromatic Dragon and the Platinum Dragon) are unique individuals. Each kind has its own entry; this section covers what they share.

Size: each of the ten species comes in three sizes (small, average, and huge). Roll d8: 1-2 small, 3-7 average, 8 huge. Size sets the dragon’s number of hit dice.

Age: dragons pass through eight ages. Roll d8 for the age, which sets the hit points per die:

d8AgeYearsHit points per die
1Very young1-51
2Young6-152
3Sub-adult16-253
4Young adult26-504
5Adult51-1005
6Old101-2006
7Very old201-4007
8Ancient401+8

Senses: all dragons see equally well by day or in darkness (infravision, 60’), and have excellent sight, smell, and hearing. These keen senses let them detect hidden or invisible creatures within 1” per age level.

Fear aura: from adult age onward, a dragon flying overhead or charging radiates a powerful aura that causes fear:

  1. All creatures under 1 hit die, and any non-carnivorous creature not trained for war or naturally fearless or aggressive, flee in panic at top speed for 4-24 turns.
  2. Creatures with fewer than 3 hit dice must save versus magic or be paralyzed with fear (50%) or flee in panic as above (50%).
  3. Creatures with 3 or more hit dice fight at −1 on their hit dice unless they also save versus magic.
  4. Creatures with 6 or more hit dice automatically ignore the aura.
  5. The aura of adult, old, and very old dragons is weaker than an ancient dragon’s, so saves against it are at +5, +3, and +1 respectively. For example, a 2nd-level fighter, who normally needs 16 (75%) or better to save against magic (here, the aura), gets +5 against an adult dragon’s aura, so any roll of 11 or more saves him from panic.

Speech and spells: many dragons speak one or more human languages besides their own, and a fair number of those can cast spells. Each species entry gives the chances for these, and the chance of a dragon being asleep.

Sleeping dragons: a sleeping dragon is found only in its lair. It always wakes on hearing loud noise (talking, shouting, forcing a door, etc.) within 30’ to 120’, depending on what muffles the sound (walls, doors, etc.) and how loud it is. It wakes if attacked, and also on a 6 on d6. Attackers get +3 to strike a sleeping dragon, but lose the bonus as soon as it wakes.

Attacking a dragon: it can be attacked to kill or to subdue. The choice must be announced before combat, or the attack is automatically to kill, and it cannot be changed for that dragon. Some attacks work better or worse against certain dragons; the number below is added to or subtracted from both the chance to hit and the damage done.

Dragon’s breathAir*Earth**Fire***Water****Electricity
Cold0−1+1−1+1
Acid0+10+10
Gas+1000
Electricity00+1−1−1
Fire−1+1−1+10
Multiple types00000

* Includes attacks by aerial servant, air elemental, djinni, invisible stalker, or “whirlwind”. ** Earth elemental, xorn, or umber hulk. *** Efreet, fire elemental, or salamander. **** Triton or water elemental.

Dragon attacks: claw/bite or breath weapon. The breath can be used at most three times per day. When there is a choice, roll percentile dice; over 50% means the dragon breathes. The breath does damage equal to the dragon’s hit points to every creature it hits (half if a saving throw is made). Cone-shaped breath is ½” across where it starts.

Subduing a dragon: attackers may choose to subdue (and so capture) a dragon if they announce it before combat. Silver, gold, chromatic, and platinum dragons cannot be subdued, and creatures of less than average intelligence cannot attack to subdue.

  • All damage scored counts as non-fatal battering and bruising.
  • At the end of each melee round, divide the total subduing damage so far by the dragon’s hit points and turn it into a percentage (0%, 1%, 35%, 99%, or whatever). Roll percentile dice; a roll equal to or under it means the dragon is subdued. It is always subdued once the subduing damage equals or exceeds its hit points (100% or more).
  • At most one human-sized attacker per 3 linear feet of exposed dragon (not counting the tail) can attack. A fully exposed dragon with a 15’ body allows at most 11 humans (5 on each flank and one at its head).

They score 44 hit points of subduing damage. Being ancient, the dragon has 8 hit points per die, and being huge it has 11 dice, for 88 hit points. The referee rolls percentile dice, needing 1% to 50%, and rolls 61%.

Round two: the dragon has just woken, so the party strikes first again. Four hit, for another 23 hit points of subduing damage. The dragon chooses to breathe (rolling 99%), turning its head and firing right where the elf, dwarf, and halfling are attacking. After saving throws they take 44, 88, and 44 hit points of damage; all three char and die. The referee works out 67 over 88, a 76% chance of subdual, but rolls 92. The dragon fights on.

Round three: the dragon wins initiative, bites, and hits the second 8th-level fighter for 23 hit points. The two fighters strike; one hits, for another 10 hit points of subdual. The chance is now 77:88 (7/8), or 87.5% (treat as 88%). The referee rolls 89.

Round four: the fighters win initiative and score 12 hit points, so the dragon is automatically subdued before it can attack. Now the looting begins.

Value of a subdued dragon: larger towns and cities usually have a market for dragons. A sold dragon usually leaves the game, though the referee may give it to one of his special non-player characters for encounters in the town or city. A subdued dragon sells for 100 to 800 gold pieces per hit point, subject to the referee’s adjustment; offers are usually decided by rolling d8. Subdued dragons can be ridden.

Length of subdual: a dragon stays subdued for an indefinite time. But if it is not strongly held, well treated, given plenty of treasure, and allowed ample freedom, it will try to kill its captor and/or escape. Several dragons: two dragons met outside their lair are a mated pair; three or more are sub-adults. Two or more met in their lair are a mated pair, with their young if any. Mated pairs are always of the 5th through 8th ages. Young in the lair are eggs (10%) or very young (90%). If the young are attacked, both adults automatically breathe and then close to bite, with a ferocity bonus of +2 to hit and +1/+3 to clawing/biting damage. If either of a mated pair is attacked, the other rushes to defend it with the same ferocity bonuses, unless it is attacked at the same time.

Treasure: very young dragons usually have none, with a 10% chance of one-quarter the listed treasure. Young dragons have a 25% chance of one-quarter the listed treasure, and sub-adults a 50% chance of one-half. Young adults and old dragons have normal treasure. Very old and ancient dragons are 50% and 75% likely to have 150% and 200% of the listed treasure, respectively.

Weaknesses: the innate cowardice of dragonkind shows in the fact that most can be subdued. Their egotism makes them open to flattery, and leads the more stupid ones to attack other powerful creatures they see as challenging their dominance. Greed and avarice drive all but the loftiest dragons (40% of silver, 80% of gold, and the platinum dragon), so very clever persons can manipulate them, as can the sight of real treasure and the promise of more.

Saving throws: once a dragon has 5 or more hit points per die, it saves as if its hit dice were its total hit points divided by 4, which is higher than its actual number. This reflects its magic resistance and general toughness. On the other hand, even a very young dragon, with only 1 hit point per die, saves according to its actual number of hit dice, for the same reason.

Chance of: speaking 100%; magic use 100%; sleeping 70%.

Tiamat rules the first plane of the Nine Hells, where she spawns all evil dragonkind. She hates all good as fiercely as she loves cruelty and hoards wealth. She is seldom (10%) outside her lair, but sometimes comes to earth to place a new dragon or seek more treasure. She can travel astrally or ethereally.

  • Attacks: she is too big to claw, but can bite with all five heads and sting with her tail at the same time, while breathing with one or more heads or casting spells with one or more heads.
  • Breath: her heads are white, black, green, blue, and red. Each breathes the weapon of that color, exactly the size and shape of that dragon’s breath, doing the damage of a huge, ancient dragon of that kind: 56 hit points of frost (cold), 64 of acid, 72 of gas (chlorine), 80 of electricity (lightning), and 88 of fire. Each breath can be used once per day.
  • Spells: each head can use two spells: the white head two 1st-level spells, the black two 2nd-level, the green two 3rd-level, the blue two 4th-level, and the red two 5th-level.
  • Damage: each head can take 16 hit points before being put out of action until it regenerates the next day. If her body takes more than 48 hit points of damage, she is dispelled to her own plane of Hell (or slain if fought in Hell), like any other devil.
  • Consorts: in her lair she always has five consort/guards: one huge, adult male dragon each of the white, black, green, blue, and red kinds. All can speak and use spells, where their kind allows.

Description: the colors of her heads run down each neck into the front of her body as stripes, gradually blending into three stripes of gray, blue-green, and purple over her back and hindquarters, which merge into a muddy dark brown tail. Her underbelly and legs are greenish white, fading into the colors of her upper body.

d8AgeYearsHit points per die
1Very young1-51

Fear aura: from adult age onward, a dragon flying overhead or charging radiates a powerful aura that causes fear:

  1. All creatures under 1 hit die, and any non-carnivorous creature not trained for war or naturally fearless or aggressive, flee in panic at top speed for 4-24 turns.
  2. Creatures with fewer than 3 hit dice must save versus magic or be paralyzed with fear (50%) or flee in panic as above (50%).
  3. Creatures with 3 or more hit dice fight at −1 on their hit dice unless they also save versus magic.
  4. Creatures with 6 or more hit dice automatically ignore the aura.
  5. The aura of adult, old, and very old dragons is weaker than an ancient dragon’s, so saves against it are at +5, +3, and +1 respectively. Speech and spells: many dragons speak one or more human languages besides their own, and a fair number of those can cast spells. Each species entry gives the chances for these, and the chance of a dragon being asleep.

Sleeping dragons: a sleeping dragon is found only in its lair. Copper dragons prefer arid rocky regions, liking warmer climates for their cavern or cave lairs. They tend to be rather selfish, so many are somewhat neutral when gain is involved.

  • Attacks: claw/claw/bite, or one of two breath weapons.
  • Acid: exactly like a black dragon’s (7” × ½”).

Gold dragons can live in any climate, but their lairs are always of solid stone, whether a cave or a castle.
