system.treasure: Individuals L, M; D, Q (× 5), S in lair
system.description:
Gnolls live and travel in greedy, loosely organized bands, with the largest dominating the rest. Bands recognize no other gnoll as supreme, but do not necessarily dislike other bands, and two or more sometimes join briefly to fight, raid, or loot, or to have a better chance against a common foe or victim. They have a so-called king, very powerful personally and with a following twice normal size, but his authority reaches only as far as his arm. They are adaptable and live almost anywhere except arctic and/or arid regions.

  • Leaders: for every 20 gnolls, a leader with 16 hit points (attacks as a 3 hit dice creature). With 100 or more, also a chieftain (armor class 3, 22 hit points, attacks as a 4 hit dice creature, 4-10 hit points damage per attack) and 2-12 guards (armor class 4, 20 hit points, attack as 3 hit dice monsters, 3-9 hit points damage).
  • Lair: always a chieftain with 5-20 guards, plus females and young equal to 50% and 200% of the males.
  • Homes: underground 85% of the time, but sometimes (15%) they take over an abandoned (or cleared) village or building. Underground they are 30% likely to have 1-3 trolls living with them as guards. Above ground they are quite likely (65%) to have 4-16 hyenas (80%) or 2-12 hyaenodons (20%) as pets and guards. They always have captives for food or slave labor (at least 1 per 10 gnolls).
  • Weapons: a great variety; all carry swords, and a typical force has:
great bow15%
pole arm35%
two-handed sword15%
battle axe20%
morning star15%
  • Allies: usually friendly with orcs, hobgoblins, bugbears, ogres, and even trolls, provided the weaker kinds are not much weaker in numbers, and the gnolls are about equal in strength to the stronger monsters.
  • Other traits: strong, but they dislike work and are poor miners. They have infravision, and speak their racial tongue, chaotic evil, troll, and often (60%) orcish and/or hobgoblin.

Description: gnolls look much like hyenas. Their skin is greenish gray, darker near the muzzle, with a reddish gray to dull yellow mane; their eyes are dull black and their nails amber. Their armor is of horn, metal plates, and leather, and like their fur capes and vests it is shabby; the furs are moth-eaten, dingy brown, black, or grayish pelts. They live short lives, 35 years on average.

system.treasure: Individuals M (× 3); C, Q (× 20) in lair
system.description:
Like their larger cousins the dwarves, gnomes are organized in clans. The clans are neither exclusive nor hostile, though there is a rivalry in which each tries to outdo the others.

Leaders:

  • For every 40 gnomes, a fighter of 2nd, 3rd, or 4th level (d6: 1-2, 3-4, or 5-6).
  • 160 or more: also a 5th-level fighter as chief and a 3rd-level fighter as lieutenant.
  • 200 or more: also a gnome cleric of 4th, 5th, or 6th level.
  • 320 or more: also a 6th-level fighter, two 5th-level fighters, a 7th-level cleric, and four 3rd-level clerics.
  • Lair: also 2-8 fighters of 2nd or 3rd level, 1-4 clerics of 2nd level, and females and young equal to 50% and 25% of the adult males. A gnome lair is sometimes in earthen burrows, but 75% of the time it is in rocky hills.

Arms: usually leather armor ringed or well studded with metal, and a shield (armor class 5), with these weapons:

short sword and short bow10%
short sword and spear20%
club and sling15%
club and spear40%
club and short sword15%
  • All gnomes above normal level have chainmail and shield; those above 5th level have plate armor and shield.
  • Higher-level fighters have a 10% chance per level of magic armor and/or weapons. Gnome clerics likewise have a 10% chance per level of 1-3 extra items usable by clerics (potion, cleric scroll, ring, wand/staff/rod, miscellaneous magic).

Guard animals: 80% likely to have tamed animals guarding the lair: 5-30 badgers (70%), 3-12 giant badgers (20%), or 2-8 wolverines (10%).

Combat: they hate kobolds and goblins, and get +1 to hit them. Gnolls, bugbears, ogres, trolls, and giants fighting gnomes subtract 4 from their rolls to hit, because of the gnomes’ small size and their skill against these much bigger creatures.

Other abilities:

  • Highly resistant to magic and poison: they save as if 4 levels above their actual level.
  • Infravision: they see monsters in the dark at 60’.
  • Mining skill: they are excellent (50% to 80% likely) at detecting passages that slope up or down, unsafe walls, floors, and ceilings, and approximate depth and direction.
  • Gnomes with magical abilities up to 4th level are rumored to exist, but this has not been proved.
  • Languages: their alignment and racial tongues, kobold, goblin, halflingish, and dwarvish, and they can speak with burrowing mammals.

Description: skin mostly wood brown, a few gray brown; hair medium to pure white; eyes gray-blue to bright blue. They wear leather and earth-toned cloth, and like jewelry. The average gnome lives 600 years.

These reclusive plant-eaters live in hilly country and defend themselves aggressively against any threat. Their weapons are two long, sharp horns, which they butt with. When charging, they add +4 to the damage they do on a hit (6-20 hit points). In rare cases they have been tamed as steeds.

If more than 7 are met, the rest are young (roll percentile dice for size, halve the number rolled, and add it to 50%).

Goblins live in tribes where the strongest rule the rest, swearing fealty to the goblin king. They may be distant relatives of kobolds. Like kobolds they like dismal surroundings, though they prefer caves and similar underground places to anywhere above ground. They too hate full daylight, attacking at −1 in sunlight, and have normal infravision (60’ range).

  • Leaders: for every 40 goblins, a leader and 4 assistants equal to orcs (7 hit points each, attacking as monsters with a full hit die). With 200 or more, also a sub-chief and 2-8 guards (each fights as a hobgoblin: 8 hit points, armor class 5, 1-8 hit points damage).
  • Wolves: any goblin force has a 25% chance that 10% of it rides huge wolves, in which case there are also 10-40 riderless wolves. A goblin lair is guarded by 5-30 huge wolves at least 60% of the time.
  • Lair: also a goblin chief and 2-8 bodyguards (9-14 hit points, armor class 4, fight as gnolls doing 2-8 hit points of damage), and females and young equal to 60% and 100% of the males (who, as usual for such creatures, do not fight). There is a 20% chance of 2-12 bugbears in the lair.
  • Weapons: usually armed with:
short sword and military pick10%
short sword and sling10%
short sword and spear10%
sling10%
morning star20%
military pick10%
spear30%

Leaders and guards usually have the best weapons, two each.

  • Other traits: fair miners, noticing new or unusual construction 25% of the time. They hate gnomes and dwarves and attack them before any other creature. All goblins take slaves and love torture.
  • Languages: their own, lawful evil, kobold, orcish, and hobgoblin.

Description: skin from yellow through dull orange to brick red; eyes reddish to lemon yellow. They wear dark leather gear and dull, soiled-looking clothing (drab brown, dirty gray, stained maroon). They live about 50 years.

Creation: a lawful good cleric of 17th or higher level can make a clay golem (a lower-level cleric can, using a magical tome). It takes a resurrection spell, an animate objects spell, a commune spell, a prayer spell, and a bless spell. The cleric first sculpts a man-shaped clay statue, then performs an uninterrupted ritual with these spells. The materials cost 20,000 gold pieces, and the vestments for the ritual at least another 30,000.

  • Control: it obeys the cleric who made it. But each melee round it fights, there is a cumulative 1% chance that a chaotic evil spirit enters it. If so, the cleric loses control forever, and it attacks every living thing, going to the nearest, killing it, and moving on to the next, until it is destroyed.
  • Attacks: as an 11 hit dice monster. Damage it does to living matter can be repaired only by a heal spell from a cleric of 17th or higher level.
  • Haste: once per day, after at least one round of combat, it can be hasted for three melee rounds, striking twice per round. (Out of control, it hastes itself at once if it has not already done so.)
  • Weapons: only blunt magical weapons, such as hammers or maces, affect it.
  • Spells: none affect it except: move earth drives it back 12” and does 3-36 hit points of damage; disintegrate slows it 50% and does 1-12 hit points; an earthquake cast directly at it stops it moving that turn and does 5-50 hit points.

Golems: general (MM)

Golems are monsters made by magic. There are four kinds, each with its own entry. All but the flesh golem are made from earthen materials; the flesh golem is made from human remains. Making a golem involves ultra-powerful spells and elemental forces.

Harming golems: magical creatures with as many hit dice as the golem, or more, can attack it with effect. To find a golem’s hit dice, count 4.5 hit points per hit die, rounding up: a flesh golem has 9 dice, a clay golem 11, a stone golem 14, and an iron golem 18.
system.hpNote: A golem’s hit dice are its hit points ÷ 4.5, rounded up (MM p.47); it attacks and saves as that many hit dice.

system.description:
Creation: by a magical tome, or by a magic-user of at least 14th level using a wish, a polymorph any object, a geas, a protection from normal missiles, and a strength spell. Materials cost 1,000 gold pieces per hit point of the golem, and it takes 1 month to make.

  • Control: its creator controls it and can have it follow simple commands (go ahead, stop, kill, etc.), or have it stay inactive until a set event happens (such as someone entering its room).
  • Berserk: in melee, there is a cumulative 1% chance per melee round that it goes berserk, attacking anything in sight at random. Its master has a 10% chance per melee round of regaining control.
  • Strength: very powerful, able to smash through doors and ordinary wooden structures. It breaks through an oak door with iron bands and hinges in 5-8 melee rounds, and does 1 point of structural damage to wooden constructions every 3 melee rounds.
  • Weapons: normal weapons do not harm it; magic weapons have normal effect.
  • Spells: most have no effect, but fire- or cold-based spells (such as wall of fire, fire ball, ice storm, etc.) slow it 50% for 2-12 melee rounds. Electrical attacks heal it 1 hit point per die of damage they would normally do (a 6-die lightning bolt heals 6 hit points of damage).

Golems: general (MM)

Golems are monsters made by magic. There are four kinds, each with its own entry. All but the flesh golem are made from earthen materials; the flesh golem is made from human remains. Making a golem involves ultra-powerful spells and elemental forces.

Harming golems: magical creatures with as many hit dice as the golem, or more, can attack it with effect. To find a golem’s hit dice, count 4.5 hit points per hit die, rounding up: a flesh golem has 9 dice, a clay golem 11, a stone golem 14, and an iron golem 18.
system.hpNote: A golem’s hit dice are its hit points ÷ 4.5, rounded up (MM p.47); it attacks and saves as that many hit dice.

system.description:
Creation: an iron golem, two-legged and man-like, is made by a magical tome or by a magic-user of 18th or higher level using wish, polymorph any object, geas, and cloud kill. Materials cost 1,000 gold pieces per hit point, and it takes 3 months to build.

  • Control: it always stays under its creator’s control and obeys any simple commands. It can stand inactive as a guard until some event happens (a door is opened, a book read, etc.).
  • Poison gas: besides striking, it breathes a cloud of poisonous gas, 1” × 1” × 1”, directly in front of it, once every 7 melee rounds.
  • Strength: three times a flesh golem’s. It does 1 point of structural damage per melee round.
  • Weapons: only magic weapons of +3 or better harm it; normal weapons and magic weapons under +3 do no damage.
  • Spells: only electrical attacks, such as lightning bolt, affect it, slowing it 50% for 3 melee rounds. Magical fire repairs its damage, 1 hit point for each hit point of fire damage.
  • Rust monsters can attack iron golems.

Golems: general (MM)

Golems are monsters made by magic. There are four kinds, each with its own entry. All but the flesh golem are made from earthen materials; the flesh golem is made from human remains. Making a golem involves ultra-powerful spells and elemental forces.

Harming golems: magical creatures with as many hit dice as the golem, or more, can attack it with effect. To find a golem’s hit dice, count 4.5 hit points per hit die, rounding up: a flesh golem has 9 dice, a clay golem 11, a stone golem 14, and an iron golem 18.
system.hpNote: A golem’s hit dice are its hit points ÷ 4.5, rounded up (MM p.47); it attacks and saves as that many hit dice.

system.description:
Creation: a man-shaped stone golem is made by a magical tome or by a magic-user of 16th or higher level using wish, polymorph any object, geas, and slow. Materials cost 1,000 gold pieces per hit point, and it takes 2 months to build.

  • Control: its creator controls it, and it understands and obeys simple commands (attack, stop, wait, go, etc.). It can be made to stand and wait to attack until someone triggers it.
  • Slow: besides its normal attack, every other melee round it can cast slow on any opponent within 1” in front of it.
  • Strength: twice a flesh golem’s. It does 1 point of structural damage every other melee round.
  • Weapons: normal weapons do not harm it; it takes weapons of +2 or better.
  • Spells: only these affect it: rock to mud slows it 50% for 2-12 melee rounds; mud to rock restores all its damage; stone to flesh makes it vulnerable to normal attacks on the next melee round.

Golems: general (MM)

Golems are monsters made by magic. There are four kinds, each with its own entry. All but the flesh golem are made from earthen materials; the flesh golem is made from human remains. Making a golem involves ultra-powerful spells and elemental forces.

Harming golems: magical creatures with as many hit dice as the golem, or more, can attack it with effect. To find a golem’s hit dice, count 4.5 hit points per hit die, rounding up: a flesh golem has 9 dice, a clay golem 11, a stone golem 14, and an iron golem 18.
system.hpNote: A golem’s hit dice are its hit points ÷ 4.5, rounded up (MM p.47); it attacks and saves as that many hit dice.

system.description:
Gorgons are bull-like creatures covered in thick metal scales, preferring remote wilderness or dreary caverns.

  • Breath: a cloud of noxious vapor that turns any creature to stone unless it makes the appropriate saving throw. It shoots out in a truncated cone, ½” across at the mouth, 6” long, and 2” across at the end. A gorgon can breathe up to 4 times per day, and always prefers this to its other attacks.
  • Other planes: its awareness, and its breath, reach into the astral and ethereal planes.

Gray ooze is a slimy horror of underground places that looks like wet stone or sedimentary cave formations. It strikes like a snake.

  • Corrosion: it eats metal as fast as a black pudding does (chainmail in a single melee round). Its acid does not harm stone or wood.
  • Defenses: spells do not harm it, and it is immune to heat and cold. Lightning and weapon blows do full damage, but weapons that strike it may corrode and break.
  • Size: large specimens (over 18 hit points) are bigger than a grown man; some (over 21 hit points) are fully 3’ wide and 12’ long, though only about 6 or 8 inches thick.
  • Psionic oozes: exceptionally large ones have a well-developed intelligence of a sort, and latent psionic ability. If psionic powers are used within 6” of one, it prepares a psychic crush of 21 to 121 psionic strength attack points and directs it at any psionic user in range. After it has launched this attack, it can be attacked psionically.

Green slimes are strange plant growths found underground. They cannot move, but grow slowly, feeding on animal, vegetable, and metal substances. They sense vibrations and often drop on creatures passing below. Huge slimes, or colonies of dozens, are sometimes reported.

  • Flesh: it attaches to living flesh and, 1-4 melee rounds later, turns the creature into green slime (no resurrection possible).
  • Wood and metal: it eats wood slowly (one inch thick per hour) but metal quickly, going through plate armor in 3 melee rounds.
  • Removal: it can be scraped off quickly (if the scraper is then thrown away), cut out, frozen, or burned. A cure disease spell kills it. Other attacks, including weapons or spells, do it no harm.

Griffons build their nests on cliffs and in rocky places, lairing in a cave if possible. They are aggressive meat-eaters whose favorite prey is horses: whenever they come within sight or smell of horseflesh (36” as a general rule), they fly to the hunt.

  • Taming: they are much sought after as fledglings, since if obtained before maturity they can be tamed as fierce, loyal steeds. Fledglings sell for 5,000 gold pieces and eggs for 2,000 on the open market.
  • Lair: 75% chance of 1 or 2 eggs or young for every 2 griffons. The young do not fight, but the adults attack until killed.

The groaning spirit, or banshee, is the spirit of an evil female elf (a very rare thing indeed), returned to harm the living. It is found only in desolate countryside, moors, etc.

  • Touch: its chilling touch does 1-8 hit points of damage per hit.
  • Wail: its more fearsome attack is its wail, or keening: everyone within 3” who hears it must save versus magic or die on the spot. It can wail only once per day, and only in darkness.
  • Sight: seeing it causes fear unless the appropriate saving throw is made.
  • Defenses: immune to charm, sleep, and hold spells, and to cold and electricity. Exorcism kills it.

* Possible in unusual characters.

Halflings are basically hard-working, orderly, peaceful citizens of communities much like human ones, though their villages usually have many burrow homes as well as surface cottages. A typical halfling lair is in pastoral countryside.

  • Leaders: for every 30 halflings, two 2nd-level fighters. More than 90: also a 3rd-level leader. More than 150: also one 4th-level fighter, two 3rd-level fighters, and three 2nd-level fighters.
  • Lair: females and children equal to 100% and 60% of the adult males, and 1-4 dogs (treat as wild dogs) per halfling.
  • Arms: usually padded or leather armor, with these weapons:
small sword and short bow10%
small sword and spear10%
short bow10%
sling20%
small sword10%
spear20%
hand axe20%
  • All halflings above normal level have armor class 6; those of 3rd or 4th level have armor class 5 and 4 respectively. All such higher-level halflings have a 10% chance per level of magic armor and/or miscellaneous weapons.
  • Resistance: they resist magic and poison, saving as if four levels higher.
  • Stealth: exceedingly good at moving quietly and hiding; they surprise on 1-4 on d6. In natural terrain with any plants to hide in, treat them as invisible.
  • They have no infravision, and they shun water.
  • Languages: their own, their alignment tongue, and common, plus gnome, goblin, and orc.

Description: ruddy-faced, with brown or sandy brown hair and brown or hazel eyes. They dress colorfully, but their trousers and coats are likely to be of practical grey, tan, or brown cloth. They live 150 years or more.

Tallfellow: taller (4’+) and slimmer, with fairer skin and hair; very rare. They wear more armor (AC 6), ride ponies, and carry more spears. Exceptionally strong tallfellows (17, 18) can reach 5th or 6th level as fighters. They speak elvish, are very friendly with elves, and live about 180 years on average.

Stout: a bit smaller (3½’+) and stockier than the typical halfling (hairfeet). They wear more armor (AC 6) and use morning stars as well as the usual halfling arms. Very strong stouts (18) can reach 5th level as fighters. Stouts have infravision, can detect sloping passages, have no fear of water, and can swim. They speak dwarvish, enjoy dwarven company, and live 200 years or more.

Harpies have the bodies of vultures but the upper bodies and heads of women. They are voracious meat-eaters and foul creatures; those living along seacoasts are usually called sirens. They speak only their own language.

  • Call: all harpies can give sweet-sounding calls. Any creature hearing them goes toward the harpies unless it saves versus magic.
  • Touch: likewise charms those who fail a saving throw versus magic. The harpies attack, torture, and devour their charmed prey, and foul with excrement whatever they do not want.
  • Attacks: vulture claws and some kind of weapon, often a bone club or a weapon left by a former victim.

Hell hounds do not normally come from the material plane, but a few now live there, brought by various creatures who wanted their evil service. Monsters and fire giants favor them as watchdogs.

  • Bite: with their great black teeth.
  • Fire breath: they also breathe scorching fire at an opponent up to 1” away, doing 1 hit point of damage per hit die, or half if the opponent saves versus dragon breath. So a 7 hit dice hell hound breathes for 7 or 4 hit points of damage per attack.
  • Stealth and senses: they move very stealthily, surprising opponents on 1-4 (out of 6). Their keen hearing means they are surprised only on a 1 (out of 6). Their exceptional sight lets them locate hidden or invisible creatures 50% of the time.

Description: rusty red to red brown, with glowing red eyes and sooty black teeth and tongues.

Herd animals live in every climate: musk oxen and reindeer at the North Pole, giraffes and antelopes at the equator. The smallest have 1 hit die, the largest 5. Their attacks are simply their ways of defending themselves (horns, butting, hooves, flight), and damage depends on the attack and the animal’s size and strength. They are not aggressive, and stampede away from whatever they think is the greatest threat. Humans or humanoids of about man-size or smaller caught in the path of a stampede are trampled to death.
system.hpNote: The smallest herd animals have 1 hit die, the largest 5 (MM p.51).

system.description: The most prized of sea steeds: strong, swift, and intelligent. Unlike a normal seahorse it has a long rear body like a great fish’s and forelegs ending in powerful fins. Fine scales cover its front parts and large scales the rest. It speaks its own language and can learn another if properly trained. Tritons often have them.

Hippogriffs live only where men do not, usually nesting on rocky crags and similar places. They fight fiercely and defend themselves resolutely.

  • Diet: they eat both plants and meat, so they are never found with pegasi. Griffons sometimes attack and eat them, but with their two great front claws and powerful beak they are not easy prey.
  • Nests: in their lair (nesting area) they attack at once. There is one nest for every 2 hippogriffs, each holding 1 or 2 eggs or fledglings. Eggs are worth 1,000 gold pieces each on the open market, fledglings 2,000 to 3,000.

Hippopotami live in the rivers and lakes of tropical regions. They eat plants, but defend their territory aggressively.

  • Bite: exceedingly strong jaws; a bull does 3-18 hit points of damage per attack.
  • Herd: 1 bull for every 4 animals (1-3 bulls in a herd).
  • Boats: if a boat or canoe passes over submerged hippopotami, there is a 50% chance a bull surfaces under it and tips it over.
  • Underwater: they travel underwater by running along the bottom, and can stay under for 15 minutes.

system.treasure: Individuals J, M, D, Q (× 5) in lair
system.description:
Tribal bands of hobgoblins may be met almost anywhere, since they are equally at home in sunlight or underground. They fight well in full daylight and have infravision (60’) to fight in total darkness too.

  • Tribes: each tribe is jealous of its status. When two tribal bands meet there will be at least catcalls and jeering (85%), and open fighting may break out (15%), unless a strong leader (a powerful monster, fighter, evil high priest, etc.) is there to control them. Hobgoblins also bully nearby orcs or goblins when they can, and hobgoblin leaders are sometimes put in goblin or orc troops to keep them in order and drive them into battle. Better known (more infamous) tribes include the Rippers, Leg Breakers, Skull Smashers, Flesh Renders, Marrow Suckers, Flayers, and Slow Killers.
  • Leaders: for every 20 hobgoblins, a leader (sergeant) and 2 assistants, with 9 hit points each. With 100 or more, also a sub-chief (armor class 3, 16 hit points, +2 damage [3-10 hit points]), who fights as a 3 hit dice monster.
  • Lair: also a chief and 5-20 bodyguards. Chiefs are armor class 2, 22 hit points, do 2-11 hit points of damage, and fight as 4 hit dice monsters; their bodyguards are like sub-chiefs. Females and young equal 150% and 300% of the males.
  • Homes: underground 80% of the time, above ground 20%. Above ground the lair is a village with a ditch, rampart, and palisade of stones, earth, and logs, two gates, and 3-6 guard towers, with dwellings usually of wood and stone mixed. Since they like to build on the ruins of humans or other more sophisticated creatures, a village may be better built than this, possibly with solid stonework, buildings, or a keep. In any case they have 2 heavy catapults, 2 light catapults, and 1 ballista per 50 warriors. Underground there is a 60% chance of 2-12 carnivorous apes as guards.
  • Weapons: typically:
sword and composite bow20%
sword and spear10%
sword and morning star5%
sword and whip5%
polearm30%
spear10%
morning star20%
  • Leaders always carry two weapons.
  • Standard: the tribal standard is with a sub-chief 20% of the time, and always with the chief. Hobgoblin warriors within 6” of it fight harder: +1 on attack rolls and +1 on morale (reaction) rolls.
  • Elves: they hate elves so much that they attack them in preference to any other troops.
  • Mining: highly skilled; they detect new construction, sloping passages, and even shifting walls 40% of the time.
  • Languages: most speak goblin, orcish, and the crude tongue of carnivorous apes, as well as their racial and alignment languages; 20% also speak common.

Description: hairy hides from dark reddish-brown to gray black; faces bright red-orange to red, with blue-red noses on large males; eyes yellowish or dark brown; teeth yellowed white to dirty yellow. They favor bright, bloody colors and black leather, and keep their weapons well polished. They live 60 years.

Koalinth: a marine hobgoblin with gills, like its land cousins in most ways. Koalinth live in caverns and sea caves in shallow water and use spears and pole arms adapted to the sea. They speak only hobgoblin and lawful evil, and prey on any creatures available. They are lighter-colored, with green faces and webbed hands and feet.

A creature made and animated by a special process involving a magic-user and an alchemist (below). It walks on its hind legs or flies.

  • Bite: 1-3 points of damage, and the victim must save versus magic or fall into a comatose sleep for 5-30 minutes.
  • Saving throws: it saves at the same level as its creator.
  • Link: it cannot speak, but knows what the magic-user knows, and the magic-user can see and hear through its eyes and ears. They share a telepathic link, and it can be controlled up to 48” from its master; it will never willingly go beyond that range.
  • Death: if it is killed, the magic-user at once takes 2-20 points of damage.

Making one: the magic-user must hire an alchemist, who needs 1-4 weeks to make the fluids for forming it, at a cost of 1 pint of the magic-user’s blood and 500-2,000 gold pieces. The magic-user must then cast mending, mirror image, and wizard eye on the fluid to form the homonculous.

Description: finished, it is man-like, about 18” tall, with greenish reptilian skin, leathery wings, and a bat-like mouth whose teeth pass on the sleep venom described above.

Horses of various kinds are found almost everywhere.

  • Panic: raging fire, sudden movement, loud noises, or strange smells panic them 90% of the time. Warhorses are only 10% likely to panic, rear, and run away.
  • War training: about 10% of ponies and wild horses can be trained for war. A pony never fights well, but is less likely to panic.
  • Warhorses fight on the second and later rounds of melee, as long as their rider stays mounted, with two hoof thrusts and a bite.
  • Loads (gold pieces of weight): the first number is the most carried at normal movement, the second the maximum load at encumbered movement. Encumbrance halves speed.
draft horse4,000/8,000
heavy warhorse5,000/7,500
light warhorse3,000/5,000
medium warhorse4,000/6,500
pony2,000/3,000
wild horse3,000/6,000

Horses (and ponies) are not agile enough to take into dungeons.

Hydrae are reptilian monsters of marshes, swamps, and similar places, and of underground lairs. Their large, four-legged bodies carry 5 to 12 heads (roll d8 for the number).

  • Heads: each head has 1 hit die of a full 8 hit points. The body dies only when every head has been killed.
  • Attacks: each head counts as a hit die, so a 7-headed hydra attacks as a 7 hit dice monster. It can attack several opponents at once, with up to 4 heads attacking the same target.
  • Damage: 5 or 6 heads, 1-6 hit points per attack; 7 to 10 heads, 1-8; 11 or 12 heads, 1-10.

Description: gray brown to blackish brown, with lighter underbellies tinged yellow or tan; amber to orange eyes; yellowish white teeth.

Lernaean hydra: very rare, and indistinguishable from a normal hydra until attacked. Every time one of its heads is cut off or killed, two new ones grow in 1-4 melee rounds, unless fire is put to the dead head or neck stump. So a 5-headed lernaean hydra could grow into a 12-headed one in a single fight, gaining the matching hit dice and attacks.

Pyrohydra: looks much like a normal hydra, though its color may be redder. It seldom has more than 7 heads; 10% have 8, and no 9-headed pyrohydra has ever been recorded. Each head can breathe fire twice per day, in a cone ½” across at the mouth, 1” across at the end, and 2” long, doing 8 hit points of damage (4 if the victim saves versus dragon breath). It can also bite normally.
system.hpNote: Each head has 1 hit die of a full 8 hit points and the body dies only when every head is killed; it attacks as a monster of as many hit dice as it has heads (MM p.53). Track each head separately. After the "roll heads" option, the number of heads is the hit points ÷ 8: set Attacks as HD to it.

system.description:
Hyenas are pack animals of warm plains: hunters and scavengers with very strong jaws, aggressive when hungry.

Hyaenodons are simply huge (prehistoric) hyenas.

Hyenas are pack animals of warm plains: hunters and scavengers with very strong jaws, aggressive when hungry.

Hyaenodons are simply huge (prehistoric) hyenas.

Imps are very rare on the material plane but not uncommon on the planes of Acheron and Hell. An imp is a very minor devil made from a larva, created to spread evil as the familiar of a lawful evil magic-user or cleric. It has average intelligence plus devilish cunning, and as a familiar can also draw on the intelligence of arch-devils.

  • Forms: it can polymorph itself at will into two of these animal forms: large spider, raven, giant rat, or goat.
  • Attacks: in its own form it strikes with its tail (hit as a dagger); any creature struck must save versus poison or die. In animal form it attacks as that animal; the raven and goat have no effective attacks.
  • Powers (in any form): detect good, detect magic, invisibility at will, regeneration of 1 hit point per melee round, and suggestion once per day.
  • Defenses: only silver or magic weapons harm it. Magical cold, fire, or electricity do not harm it, and against spells it counts as a 7 hit dice creature.

As a familiar, it gives its “master”:

  • a telepathic link, through which the master receives all the imp’s senses, including infrared vision, up to a mile away;
  • within 1”: 25% magic resistance and regeneration of 1 hit point per melee round;
  • within 1 mile: one extra level of ability; over a mile away, the master loses 1 level, and if the imp is killed the master drops 4 levels;
  • besides its normal help and advice, once per week the imp can contact a lower plane to help its master decide on a course of action, like a commune spell but with 6 questions.

One of the most feared monsters, found deep underground or in dark, dismal lairs in the wilderness. Its awareness extends to the astral and ethereal planes, and it often roams them. It can speak any human language.

  • Hunting: it can attack with its great claws, but its main weapon is psionic, since it lives on its prey’s psychic energy, whether from the dying shriek or by subtler means. If psionic energy (from abilities or magic) is used within 6”, it stalks the user, waiting to catch him alone and by surprise. Then it leaps on him, tearing with its claws and attacking psionically with ego whip or id insinuation.
  • Possession: if its psionic attack succeeds, it moves into the now mindless body and tries to fool others by acting as the person it has slain, while looking for chances to attack and devour others.
  • Stealth: it hides in shadows as well as a 10th-level thief.
  • Defenses: normal weapons and most spells have no effect. Magic weapons of +3 or better do 1 point of damage when they hit. Bright light drives it off, and protection from evil keeps it at a distance. Fireball acts only as a bright light, but lightning bolt causes it pain and a little damage (1 point per die of the bolt). Death spell has a 25% chance of working, and power word kill slays it.
  • Psionic attack: it can be attacked psionically, and with its total psionic strength of 200 this is not too difficult. If seriously threatened, it tries to flee and save itself.

A creature from the elemental plane of air, normally met on the material plane only when a magic-user conjures one to serve on this plane for a time. They roam the astral and ethereal planes, and can be dimly seen there and on the elemental planes.

  • Invisible: elsewhere, unless opponents can detect/see invisible objects, opponents subtract 2 from their “to hit” rolls.
  • Death: unless slain on its own plane, a stalker whose damage exceeds its hit points is simply sent back to the elemental plane.
  • Service: the conjurer keeps full command until it completes its duties or is killed. Given a mission, it follows through relentlessly until it is done. It is a faultless tracker up to one day after its quarry passes, and must be destroyed to stop an ordered attack. When the mission is finished, it is free to return to its own plane.
  • Twisting orders: it is at best an unwilling servant, though it does not resent a brief, simple task. A week of service tries it severely, and anything longer is sure to make it try to obey the letter of the command while twisting its spirit. Longer service is possible, but the compulsion must be great (a carefully worded command from a very powerful magic-user). “Follow me, and guard me from any attack” could be read as following 100’ behind, if it had been on duty more than a week, or even sooner, since dealing with these creatures is always a hazard. “Keep me safe from all harm” could be taken to mean carrying the conjurer to its own plane and putting him in suspended animation in a secret room of its home, obeying to the letter.
  • Each day of duty adds a cumulative 1% chance that it tries to twist its commands to win its freedom. If it has no way to do so, it must keep serving.
  • Language: it understands common but speaks only its own language.

These moose-sized creatures of the Pleistocene epoch live in temperate climates. Their antlers spread 10’ wide, and they can gore two opponents within that span if both are directly in front of the deer. They are not usually aggressive, but are very dangerous in the rutting season (early spring).

Ixitxachitl are a race of intelligent rays living in shallow tropical seas. They are evil, and clerical in nature.

  • Clerics: for every 10, one casts spells as a 2nd-level human cleric; for every 20, one as 3rd level; for every 50, one as 5th level. With more than 50, there are also a leader with 8th-level cleric spells and four times normal hit dice, and two guards with 6th-level cleric spells and triple normal hit dice.
  • Vampiric ixitxachitl: for every 20 met there is a 50% chance of a vampiric one in the group. It is like the others, but has double hit dice, regenerates 3 hit points per melee round, and drains an energy level each time it strikes an opponent.
  • Lair: hard to find, usually in a coral reef behind a secret entrance. It holds items as for treasure types P, R, and S. A leader and its guards may have type U magic items that can be worn, or used without hands, if they are in their lair.
Jackals are small, dog-like scavengers of warm regions, neither particularly fierce nor brave. They appear here because of the magical bag of tricks.

The jackalwere is a malign enemy of humankind: a jackal that can take the form of a man. In that guise it roams about seeking to waylay and murder humans, then steals their riches and eats them. It can use human weapons. Its gaze works as a sleep spell on any unsuspecting creature that fails a saving throw versus magic (a hostile creature is not unsuspecting!). Jackalweres are sometimes (20%) found with normal jackals.

These very ferocious jungle predators attack any creature they think threatens them. When hungry they hunt prey much larger than themselves, including snakes and crocodiles. They climb well, swim well, and can leap 30’ to attack.

  • Rake: in close combat, if both forepaws hit in the same melee round, the jaguar grips its opponent and rakes with its rear claws: 2 more attacks that turn, each doing 2-5 hit points.
  • Lair: 75% chance of 1-3 young (10% to 40% grown), who do not fight effectively.

The ki-rin are a race of sky creatures whose hooves rarely touch the earth; they live among the clouds and behind the winds. Females are never met, and ki-rin are always solitary. They sometimes help humans if properly entreated, or if the need to fight evil is great. They sometimes travel the astral and ethereal planes.

  • Attacks: two powerful hoof blows and a thrust with a magically sharp (+3) horn much like a unicorn’s. They can attack in other ways as well.
  • Spells: spells of all levels at 18th-level quality, each day: 9 of 1st level, 8 of 2nd, 7 of 3rd, 6 of 4th, 5 of 5th, 4 of 6th, 3 of 7th, 2 of 8th, and 1 of 9th.
  • Psionics: 4 major and 6 minor disciplines, all at ninth level of mastery.
  • Once per day each: create nutritious food for 2-24 persons; create drinkable beverages for 2-24 persons; create permanent soft goods or wooden items (up to 32 cubic feet of soft goods or 18 cubic feet of wood); create fairly short-lived metal items of up to 2,000 gold pieces weight (from gold lasting 2-5 days to adamantite lasting only 1 hour); create an illusion with sound, sight, and smell that lasts without concentration until magically dispelled or touched in disbelief; assume gaseous form; wind walk; call lightning; and summon weather.
  • Sky magic: things of the sky, or involving air, that a ki-rin conjures are at twice normal strength, including hit points and damage.
  • Language: their own tongue, and a special telepathic speech that lets them talk with almost any living thing.

Description: a coat of luminous gold, like sunrise on a clear day; darker gold mane and tail; golden pink horn and hooves; violet eyes. (A perfectly intact ki-rin skin is worth 25,000 gold pieces.)

system.treasure: Individuals J, O, Q (× 5) in lair
system.description:
Kobold society is tribal, with war bands based on gens; stronger tribes rule weaker ones. Kobolds are usually found in dank, dark places, such as dismal overgrown forests or underground. They hate bright sunlight, in which they cannot see well (−1 on their rolls to hit there), but their night vision is excellent, with infravision that works well up to 60’.

  • Leaders: for every 40 kobolds, a leader and two guards equal to goblins (4 hit points each, armor class 6, 1-6 points of damage).
  • Lair: always a chief and his bodyguard. With 200 or more kobolds, there are also 5-20 guards (as the bodyguards above), females equal to 50% of the total, young equal to 10% of the total, and 30-300 eggs. It is also probable (65%) that 2-5 wild boars (70%) or 1-4 giant weasels (30%) guard the lair.
  • Weapons: a kobold force is typically equipped as follows:
short sword and javelin5%
short sword and spear10%
short sword10%
axe20%
spiked wooden club30%
javelins (2-3)15%
spear10%

Chiefs and guards always have the best weapons available. All kobold shields are of wood or wickerwork.

  • Nature: they hate most other life and delight in killing and torture. They particularly hate brownies, pixies, sprites, and gnomes, and are constantly at war with gnomes, attacking them on sight.
  • Languages: lawful evil and kobold, and usually (75%) goblin and orcish.

Description: hide from very dark rusty brown to rusty black, with no hair; reddish eyes; small tan to white horns. They favor red or orange clothing, and live up to 135 years.

Lamias prefer deserts, living in ruined cities, caves, or the like. Their upper body, arms, and head are like a human woman’s; their lower body is a beast’s. They are very fast and powerful, and usually armed with daggers. They speak their alignment language and common.

  • Spells (once per day each): charm person, mirror image, suggestion, and illusion (as a wand), usually used to lure people to the lamia and hold them there to be devoured.
  • Touch: permanently drains 1 point of wisdom. When a victim’s wisdom drops below 3, he willingly does whatever the lamia says.
  • Feeding: lamias first drain their prey’s blood, then feast on the flesh.

Lammasu live in warm regions but sometimes visit every climate. By nature they help and protect lawful good persons, and are kind and friendly toward all good creatures. They speak their own tongue and the language of lawful good, and use a limited form of telepathy.

  • At will: invisibility and/or dimension door.
  • Protection: they radiate a double-strength protection from evil in a 10’ radius (−2 on evil attacks, +2 on saving throws against evil attacks).
  • Spells: cleric spells up to 4th level, at 6th-level ability: 4 of 1st level, 3 of 2nd, 2 of 3rd, and 1 of 4th. Their cure wounds spells have double effect (4-14 and 8-28). 10% can also speak a holy word.

Lampreys are leech-like eels living in fresh and salt water, though not in shallow water. They feed by biting their victims and fastening on with round, sucking mouths ringed with cruel teeth. Starting on the next melee round, and every round after, an attached lamprey drains blood equal to 2 hit points of damage per hit die it has; a giant one drains 10 hit points per melee round.

Lampreys are leech-like eels living in fresh and salt water, though not in shallow water. They feed by biting their victims and fastening on with round, sucking mouths ringed with cruel teeth. Starting on the next melee round, and every round after, an attached lamprey drains blood equal to 2 hit points of damage per hit die it has; a giant one drains 10 hit points per melee round.

Larvae are the most selfishly evil of all the souls that sink to the lower planes after death. They live in the gloom of Hades, controlled by the night hags. Demons and devils both want them, to make quasits and imps respectively, and liches use their essence to keep their undead status and powers. Because larvae are so valuable, the night hags trade them to keep their planes free.

Larvae look like sickly yellow worms with distorted human faces.

Found only in the fetid waters of swamps and marshes, giant leeches threaten any warm-blooded creature passing within their 3” movement range. They wait in the mud and slime and strike as prey goes by. They range from 1 to 4 hit dice, and different sizes are usually found together.

  • Draining: the first attack also attaches the leech’s sucker mouth. On the next melee round, and every round after, it drains blood equal to 1 hit point of damage per hit die.
  • Unnoticed: its saliva numbs, so unless the victim leaves the water there is only a 1% chance it notices the attack. Bite and draining usually go unfelt until weakness (loss of 50% of hit points) tells the victim something is wrong.
  • At night giant leeches come out of the water to attack prey within 3”.
  • Killing: by attack, or by sprinkling plenty of salt on them.
  • Disease: 50% chance the bite causes disease, fatal in 2-5 weeks unless cured.
system.hpNote: Different sizes are usually found together (MM p.60).

system.description:
These meat-eaters live in tropical woodlands and jungles. They hunt by lying in wait and leaping on their prey, surprising on 1-3. They can spring 20’ up or 25’ ahead.

  • Rake: if both forepaws hit in a melee round, the leopard gets 2 more attacks that round, each doing 1-4 hit points of damage.
  • Lair: 25% chance of 1-3 cubs, who have no effective attack.

Leprechauns normally live only in fair, green lands with lush hills and dales to frolic in, though now and then an adventurous party of them lives elsewhere for a time. These small, magically talented, mischievous creatures are rumored to be a kind of halfling with a strong strain of pixie.

  • At will, as often as they like: invisibility, polymorph non-living objects, create illusions, and ventriloquism.
  • Senses: their keen ears mean they are never surprised.
  • Theft: full of mischief, they often (75%) snatch a valuable object from someone, turn invisible, and dash off. Such a theft is 75% likely to succeed. If closely pursued, there is a 25% chance per turn of pursuit that the leprechaun drops the stolen goods.
  • Treasure: if caught, or found in its lair, a leprechaun tries to fool its captor into believing he is being given its treasure while actually duping him. Getting the treasure takes great care.
  • Weakness: they are very fond of wine, which can be used to outwit them.

This weird creature haunts deserted and desolate places, since it is so ugly most creatures cannot bear the sight of it. Its body is like a stag’s, with a rather lion-like tail and legs ending in cloven hooves. Its head is a huge badger’s, but with sharp, jagged bony ridges instead of teeth. It speaks its alignment language and common.

  • Mimicry: very sly, it imitates a man’s or woman’s voice to trick prey into coming within reach.
  • Kick: when retreating it can kick backward with both hooves, each doing 1-6 hit points of damage on a hit.

system.psionicText: See below Attack/Defense Modes: See below
system.description:
A lich exists by its own will and the use of powerful, arcane magic: through force of will it passes from humanity into a non-human, non-living existence, kept up by certain conjurations, enchantments, and a phylactery. Liches were once ultra-powerful magic-users or magic-user/clerics of at least 18th level of magic use. A lich is most often met in its hidden chambers, usually in some wilderness area or vast underground labyrinth, always solidly built of stone and very dark.

  • Armor and hit dice: the power that changed it makes its armor class equal to +1 plate armor and +1 shield (armor class 0), and its hit dice are 8-sided.
  • Harming it: only magical attacks, or monsters with magical properties or 6 or more hit dice, can affect it.
  • Touch: so cold it does 1-10 points of damage and paralyzes those who fail their saving throw.
  • Fear: merely seeing a lich makes any creature below 5th level (or 5 hit dice) flee in panic.
  • Spells: it can use magic appropriate to the level it had reached before ceasing to be human.
  • Immunities: charm, sleep, enfeeblement, polymorph, cold, electricity, insanity, and death spells or symbols have no effect.

Description: much like a wight or mummy: skeletal, its eye sockets black holes with glowing points of light, its garments usually rotting (but very rich).
system.hpNote: Hit dice 11+, 8-sided: use the level it had reached as a magic-user (or magic-user/cleric) (MM p.61).

system.description:
Lions generally live in warmer climates, warm temperate to tropical, and thrive anywhere from desert to jungle, swamp to savannah. They hunt in prides; the males seldom do any actual stalking or killing, since the lioness is the real huntress. But males are ferocious fighters and actively defend the group’s territory.

  • Armor: males are armor class 5 in front and armor class 6 behind; lionesses are armor class 6.
  • Leap: all can spring up to 30’.
  • Rake: if a lion scores two paw hits in melee, it rakes with its two rear claws that turn, each doing 2-7 points of damage.
  • Pride: typically 1-3 males and 1-9 females. In the lair there are 1-10 cubs (30% to 60% grown) who do not fight, with 1-4 lionesses who attack at once.
  • Lions do not climb trees well and dislike swimming.

Mountain lion: not a true lion but a kind of great cat, living in forests and deserts as well as mountains. Somewhat cautious, but a fierce fighter if threatened or cornered. It can spring 15’ up or at least 20’ ahead to attack, and each rear claw rakes for 1-4 hit points of damage.

Spotted lion: also called cave lions, these are larger, spotted common lions. They roam the plains of the Pleistocene epoch, with few found elsewhere. Their hunting habits and groups are much like those of their smaller, more modern kin.

They hunt in prides; the males seldom do any actual stalking or killing, since the lioness is the real huntress. But males are ferocious fighters and actively defend the group’s territory.

system.specialAttacks: See below for each type of lizard
system.description:
Fire lizard: these reptiles may be an ancestral dragon type, or an offshoot of a common ancestor. They look like red dragons and are sometimes called “false dragons”; red dragons seem to avoid them.

  • Habits: slow-moving, and often (50%) asleep for long periods. They live in underground lairs, coming out every fortnight or so to hunt. Shiny things attract them, so they collect metals and gems in their dens.
  • Eggs: 10% chance of 1-4 eggs in the lair (market value 5,000 gold pieces each). The lizard does not otherwise care for its young, which leave after hatching.
  • Attacks: usually two raking claws and a bite, but it can also breathe a puff of flame: a truncated cone ½” across at the mouth, 1” across at the end, and 1½” long, doing 2-12 hit points of damage (1-6 on a successful save). Fire attacks do not harm it.
  • Color: usually neutral gray, mottled red brown on the back, with reddish undersides. Young ones are lighter, old ones (50 to 100 years) darker.

Giant lizard: remarkable only for its size; it prefers marshes and swamps. Its large mouth can engulf prey: a “to hit” roll of 20 means it has clamped both jaws on its opponent, doing double damage (2-16 hit points).

Minotaur lizard: huge, very aggressive meat-eaters, usually found only in warm regions. They move slowly, but hide and snatch quickly at prey, surprising on 1-4. Their long, sharp talons and teeth cause terrible wounds, and they drag subdued prey into their dens to eat at leisure. Because of their mouth size, a roll of 20 means the lizard has picked up a creature of man-size and weight or less (7’ or less, 300 pounds or less) and holds it fast in its mouth, where it is helpless to attack next round and the lizard is sure to be able to bite it again.

Subterranean lizard: a giant lizard found only underground, most aggressive and dreaded, since its suction-cupped toes let it run along ceilings or walls as easily as floors. Worse, its horrible teeth cause great wounds, and on a roll of 20 it clamps both jaws firmly on its victim for double damage. Like most lizards, it usually drags its prey to its lair before eating it.

Lizard men are semi-aquatic. They breathe air, but often (35%) live completely underwater, lairing in caves that are not flooded. They are usually found in swamps, marshes, and similar places, banded together in rough tribes, and speak their own language.

  • Diet: they eat both plants and meat, but are likely to prefer human flesh. They have been known to ambush humans, gather up the dead and the survivors, and take them all back to their lair for a crude and horrid feast.
  • Advanced tribes: about 1 tribe in 10 has evolved further. These live in crude huts, use shields (armor class 4), and throw barbed darts (3” range, 1-4 points of damage) or javelins (1-6 hit points of damage) before closing with enemies. In melee they use clubs (treat as morning stars).

The locathah are a humanoid race of sea nomads who roam shallow seas, hunting and gathering food in bountiful warm waters.

  • Leaders: for every 40 locathah, a leader with 18 hit points (treat as a 4th-level fighter) and 4 assistants with 14 hit points (treat as 3rd-level fighters). With more than 120, also a chief with 22 hit points (treat as a 5th-level fighter) and 12 guards (12-14 hit points, 3rd-level fighters).
  • Mounts: they always ride giant eels, which also fight (see EEL for statistics).
  • Weapons: a typical force is armed as follows:
lance20%
crossbow30%
trident30%
net & dagger20%
  • Lair: usually a castle-like undersea rock hollowed out into rooms, passages, etc., guarded by stout doors and 4-16 moray eels as warders, with a 50% chance of a Portuguese man o’ war trap as well.

Description: scaled in pale yellow hues. Their ears are fanned with fins to hear better, and their large eyes see better in the water. Their back scales and fins are darker than those in front.

A meat-eating creature found only underground. Usually only 1 is met, though a large chamber or cave might hold as many as 4. Being unintelligent, it fights until dead.

  • Movement: it can creep slowly along surfaces (1”), or fill sacs around its body with a gas it makes, giving it neutral buoyancy so it can fly about by flapping its wing-like edges.
  • Hiding: it looks somewhat like a large manta ray. Its grayish belly is textured to look like stone, and it usually clings to a ceiling, where it is almost impossible to detect (90%) unless actually prodded. It surprises prey on 1-4 (on d6).
  • Attack: when disturbed it drops from the ceiling, smothering everything beneath it in the tough folds of its “wings”. The squeezing does 1-6 points of damage per round, and the victims smother in 2-5 rounds in any case unless they kill it and break free. Caught prey can fight back only with weapons that are both short and already in hand when it falls.

system.description:
Lycanthropes are humans who can take animal form. They most often change to animal form during the hours of darkness, and during a full moon they are 90% likely to be forced to take their other shape. Usually they move about as humans, for whatever purposes they have. Each kind has its own language, spoken as well as common. Other kinds of lycanthrope exist, but they are extremely rare.

Catching lycanthropy: any humanoid bitten by a lycanthrope for damage equal to 50% or more of its total hit points, but not actually killed (and eaten), is infected with the disease of lycanthropy.

  • If the victim carries belladonna and eats it within one hour, there is a 25% chance it cures the disease. The dose incapacitates the person for 1-4 days and has a 1% chance of killing him.
  • Otherwise, a cure disease spell from a patriarch of 12th or higher level must be cast on the victim within 3 days, or he becomes a lycanthrope in 7-14 days.

Werebear: great werebears are the most powerful lycanthropes, and are never met except full-grown. A werebear alone is 50% likely to be with 1-6 brown bears, and can summon 1-6 brown bears in 2-12 turns if any are within one mile. In human form it is usually large, hairy, and solitary. Werebears heal three times as fast as normal, are immune to disease, and can cure disease in another creature in 1-4 weeks if they wish.

Wereboar: found in dense woodlands and similar areas; ugly-tempered and likely to attack. In human form they are usually hot-tempered and irritable, typical berserkers. They seldom mix with normal boars (15% chance).

Wererat: sometimes called ratmen, these sly, evil creatures live in tunnel complexes under cities. They have three forms: human, human-sized ratman, and giant rat. Usually armed with swords. They use human form to fool humans, luring them somewhere they can be captured and held for ransom or perhaps eaten. They prefer to move about in rat-like form, smaller than a man but much larger than a normal rat. Each can summon and control 2-12 giant rats.

Weretiger: much like normal tigers in where they live, and most often female. Only 5% likely to mix with normal cats, but they can speak with all kinds of cats, so cats are 75% likely to be friendly with them.

Werewolf: in human form werewolves are very hard to detect, since they can be of almost any build and of either sex. Werewolves tend to stay two-legged in wolf form, but wolfweres (wolves that can become men) always take normal wolf form. Both kinds are likely to be found in packs.

  • Family packs: a pack of 5 to 8 may be a family: a male, a female, and 3 to 6 young of 60% to 90% growth.
  • If the female is attacked, the male fights at +2 to hit and does full damage with each hit.
  • If the cubs are attacked, the female fights at +3 to hit and does full possible damage with each hit.
  • The young fight at −4 to −1 to hit, by maturity, doing 2-5 points of damage per attack.

These forest cats prefer cold regions. They are aggressive, and their intelligence lets them compete well with other predators. They speak their own language.

  • Movement: they climb very well, swim reasonably well, and can leap 15’.
  • Rake: if both forepaws hit, the lynx gets two more attacks, raking with its rear claws for 1-3 hit points each.
  • Stealth: they have learned to hide to avoid detection (90% unlikely to be seen in normal circumstances) or to surprise prey (surprise on 1-5).
  • Traps: 75% accurate at detecting traps.
  • Lair: 25% chance of 1-4 kittens (10% to 30% grown) with no effective attack.

There are several kinds of mammoth, including the woolly and the imperial (the largest). They live in climates from subarctic to subtropical in the Pleistocene epoch. These massive plant-eaters are quite aggressive if threatened.

  • Attacks: like elephants and mastodons, a mammoth has 5 attack forms, but generally can use no more than 2 against a single opponent.
  • Tusks: 50% heavier than an elephant’s, and worth proportionately more.

Manticores prefer dismal lairs, so they are usually found in caves or underground. They range in all climates, though they like warm places more than cold. Their favorite prey is man, and they are usually met outside their lairs hunting human victims.

  • Tail spikes: a manticore opens an attack by firing a volley of 6 iron spikes from its tail (18” range, as a light crossbow, 1-6 hit points of damage per hit). It can fire four such volleys.

Description: each part has the color it should: a lion-colored body, bat-brown wings, and a head of human flesh.

These worm-like fish move slowly along coral reefs, crushing and eating the coral. If surprised or threatened, they tend to attack in “self defense”.

  • Spines: each has 4, 6, or 8 dorsal spines, 4’ long, with poisonous secretions. Unless it is fought from directly in front or below, it can thrust these spines out to block attacks, and anyone stuck by one must save versus poison or be killed.

Mastodons live in almost any climate, from near arctic to tropical, and are common on Pleistocene plains. These huge plant-eaters are distant relatives of elephants, with somewhat lower, longer bodies.

  • Attacks: 5 attack modes (2 tusks, 1 trunk, 2 forefeet), but no more than 2 at a time against a single opponent. For the limits and other details see ELEPHANT.
  • Tusks: the same weight and value as an elephant’s.

Medusae are hateful humanoid creatures that live in dark caves or caverns and sometimes come out to seek prey, trying to trick humans into looking into their eyes. They speak their own tongue and common.

  • Gaze: turns creatures within 3” to stone unless they save versus petrifaction. It can see astral and ethereal creatures, and its gaze works on those planes as well as on the material one. If its gaze is reflected back at it, the medusa turns itself to stone!
  • Asps: if an opponent looks away, the medusa rushes up so its asp-like hair can bite. The bite has a range of only 1’, and the victim must save versus poison or die.

Description: its body looks quite shapely and human, and it usually wears human clothes. But its face is horrible and its snaky hair writhes, which gives it away at close range (20’). Its glaring, red-rimmed eyes are clearly visible at 30’.

system.psionicText: Leader types Attack/Defense Modes: Leader types
system.description:
Bandits roam every climate from temperate to subtropical, traveling in groups usually led by high-level fighters, magic-users, and clerics. Those met in dungeons are far fewer and often work with thieves.

  • Extra fighters: for every 20 bandits, a 3rd-level fighter; for every 30, a 4th-level; for every 40, a 5th-level; for every 50, a 6th-level.
  • Leader: always an 8th-, 9th-, or 10th-level fighter (8th with under 100 bandits, 9th with 100 to 150, 10th with 150 or more), with a 7th-level lieutenant and 6 guards of 2nd level. These 8 are in addition to the number rolled.
  • Magic-user: for every 50 bandits, a 25% chance of a magic-user of 7th, 8th, 9th, or 10th level (roll d4 for level). So 200 bandits always have one.
  • Cleric: for every 50 bandits, a 15% chance of a cleric of 5th or 6th level, with a 3rd- or 4th-level assistant (roll only for the former).
  • Lair: an informal camp 80% of the time, a cave complex with a secret entrance 10%, or a regular castle with 1-4 light catapults 10%. It holds 2-20 important prisoners and 5-30 camp followers/slaves.
  • Psionics: leaders have normal chances of psionic ability.

Mounts, armor, and arms:

medium horse, chainmail & shield, sword10%
light horse, leather armor & shield, spear10%
light horse, leather armor, light crossbow10%
leather armor & shield, sword40%
leather armor, pole arm10%
leather armor, light crossbow10%
leather armor, short bow10%

Terrain changes the share of mounted bandits: in hills and mountains no more than 10% are horsed, while in open country 90% are.

Brigands: chaotic evil bandits, like bandits in general except: their lair is a cave complex 20% of the time and a castle 30%; they hold only 1-10 important prisoners but 20-50 camp followers/slaves; and their high morale gives them +1 on reaction (morale) rolls.

Example of bandits (or brigands):

Number encountered:110
horsed33
afoot77

Additional high-level fighters:

3rd level5
4th level3
5th level2
6th level1
leader, 9th level1
lieutenant, 7th level1
guards, 2nd level6
Total130
chance for a magic-user50%
chance for 2 clerics30%

Men: general (MM)

Normal men have 1-6 hit points each. Many kinds of men are often met in the wilderness or in dungeons, always in groups; as a general rule, smaller bands underground and larger ones outdoors. Each kind has its own entry.

  • Leaders: any group of men always includes higher-level characters; each entry gives the exact number.
  • Equipment: higher-level fighters, and clerics too, usually ride unbarded medium warhorses and wear plate armor and shield.
  • Psionics: high-level leaders have the usual chance of psionic abilities.

Magic items: each higher-level fighter, magic-user, and cleric has a 5% chance per level of having magic items in each category marked “yes” below. Roll for each “yes”. If a cursed or otherwise undesirable item comes up, reroll once only; if no usable item results, there is no item in that category.

FighterMagic-userClericThief
Armoryesnoyesno
Shieldyesnoyesyes
Swordyesnonoyes
Miscellaneous weaponyesnoyes*yes
Potionyesnoyesyes
Scrollnoyesyesno
Ringnoyesnoyes
Wand/staff/rodnoyesno*no
Miscellaneous magicnoyesyesyes

* If no miscellaneous weapon is found, or the one found has an edge, roll again for a possible wand/staff/rod; if one is found but a cleric cannot use it, he has no such item.

Example: a 6th-level cleric is checked. He has a 30% chance each for magic armor, shield, miscellaneous weapon, potion, scroll, and miscellaneous magic item. Rolling percentile dice for each, he succeeds for shield, miscellaneous weapon, and scroll. The first shield rolled is cursed, but the reroll gives a +1 shield. For the miscellaneous weapon he gets magic arrows, which he cannot use, so a roll on the wand/staff/rod table is called for; the item it gives is also not usable by him, so that category is dropped. Finally, the scroll table gives him a protection from undead scroll.

Berserkers are bands of fighters who gather to go looking for battle. They scorn armor and fight mad with battle lust, which lets them strike twice, or once at +2 to hit. They never check morale: if they decide a fight would bring them honor (and possibly loot), they attack.

  • Extra fighters: for every 10 berserkers, a 1st-level fighter; for every 20, a 2nd-level; for every 30, a 3rd; for every 40, a 4th; for every 50, a 5th. All are in addition to the number rolled.
  • Leaders: a war chief and two sub-chieftains: 9th and 6th level with 60 or fewer berserkers, 10th and 7th level with more than 60.
  • Cleric: for every 10 berserkers, a 50% chance of a 7th-level berserk cleric with 1-4 assistants of 3rd or 4th level.

system.description:
Buccaneers sail the oceans, seas, large lakes, and broad rivers of the world. Their armor depends on where they are. They are usually met in their lair, which is their ship(s); only 20% of the time are they met ashore along some coast.

  • Extra fighters: for every 50 buccaneers a 3rd-level fighter, and for every 100 a 5th-level fighter, in addition to the number rolled.
  • Leaders: always a captain of 8th or 10th level (8th if fewer than 200 buccaneers), with a lieutenant of 6th or 7th level and 4 mates of 4th level, in addition to the regular buccaneers.
  • Spell casters: for every 50 buccaneers, a 15% chance of a cleric of 12th, 13th, 14th, or 15th level, and a 10% chance of a magic-user of 6th, 7th, or 8th level.
  • Prisoners: 2-5 held in the lair for ransom.

Armor and arms:

chainmail & shield, sword, hand axe5%
chainmail & sword5%
leather armor & shield, sword10%
leather armor & spear30%
leather armor & axe20%
leather armor & heavy crossbow10%
leather armor & light crossbow20%

Cavemen are primitive, very fierce humans found where no other humans live.

  • Leaders: for every 10 cavemen, a 3rd-level fighter. Always led by a 5th-level fighter (chief) with 1-4 4th-level sub-chiefs, all in addition to the number rolled. For every 10 cavemen there is a 10% chance of a 3rd-level cleric (also a caveman, but with normal cleric spells).
  • Lair: always in caves or caverns, with females and young equal to 100% and 50% of the males.
  • Treasure: allow a 5% chance per 10 cavemen each for ivory tusks, gold nuggets, or uncut gems; if any one is found, there is no other treasure. Ivory: 2-12 tusks, each worth 1,000 gold pieces and needing 2 men to carry. Gold nuggets: 20-80, each the size of 5 gold pieces. Uncut gems: 1-100, of base 10 gold piece value.
  • Arms:
spear & stone axe10%
stone axe20%
club50%
spear20%
  • Treat stone axes as battle axes and clubs as morning stars. Being strong, cavemen add +1 to damage rolls.
  • The unknown tends to frighten them: subtract 1 from reaction rolls in such morale checks.

Tribesmen: primitive tribesmen are usually found in tropical jungles or on islands. They use large shields.

  • Leaders: as cavemen, plus 1 4th-level cleric for every 10 tribesmen, 1 6th-level cleric for every 30 tribesmen, and 1 8th-level head cleric (witchdoctor). Their clerics are druidical.
  • Village: huts of grass, bamboo, or mud, with a 50% chance of a log palisade. Females and young each equal 100% of the males. 75% chance of 20-50 slaves, and 50% chance of 2-12 captives (food!) held in a pen.
  • Treasure: exactly as cavemen, except tribesmen can have all three types.
  • Arms:
shield, spear & club30%
shield & 2 spears40%
shortbow & club30%

Treat tribesmen’s clubs as maces.

system.description:
Dervishes are highly religious nomads (see below), met only in deserts or steppes/plains.

  • Extra fighters: for every 30 dervishes, a 3rd-level fighter; for every 40, a 4th; for every 50, a 5th; for every 60, a 6th.
  • Leader: a cleric of 10th, 11th, or 12th level (10th with under 125, 11th with under 250, 12th with 250 or more), with 2 assistant clerics of 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, or 8th level as his personal bodyguard. All are in addition to the number rolled.
  • Magic-users: for every 50 dervishes, a 15% chance of a magic-user of 7th or 8th level with two assistants of 3rd or 4th level, in addition to the others. With more than 200 dervishes, the magic-users are of the higher levels.
  • Lair: a walled fortress holding 200 to 300 dervishes, defended by 1-4 ballistae, 1-4 light catapults, and 1-2 heavy catapults.
  • Fanatics: dervishes add 1 to their rolls to hit and for damage, and never check morale in combat.
  • Leaders’ armor: chainmail, so any magic armor rolled is chain. Leaders have normal chances of psionic abilities.

medium warhorse, chainmail & shield, lance, sword25%
medium warhorse, chainmail & shield, composite bow, sword5%
light warhorse, leather armor & shield, lance, sword50%
light warhorse, leather armor & shield, composite bow, sword10%
light warhorse, leather armor & shield, light crossbow, mace10%

Nomads: bands of desert or steppes/plains dwellers who roam freely, herding and hunting. They use terrain to hide so well that they surprise on 1-4.

  • Extra fighters: as dervishes. They have normal chances of psionic abilities.
  • Leaders: a fighter of 8th, 9th, or 10th level (8th with under 150 nomads, 9th with 150-250, 10th with 250 or more), with a sub-commander of 6th, 7th, or 8th level and 12 guards of 2nd level, in addition to the number rolled.
  • Spell casters: for every 50 nomads, a 15% chance of a cleric of 4th-7th level, and the same chance of a magic-user of 5th-8th level. Whatever those rolls show, a band always has 2 3rd-level clerics and a 4th-level magic-user.
  • Lair: 90% likely to be an encampment of tents (or yurts and carts) at an oasis or stream, with females equal to 200% of the males, children equal to 100%, 10-100 slaves, 100-400 horses, and twice that many herd animals (sheep, goats, camels, cattle, and/or yaks). 10% of the time it is a small walled city, with 20-80 more footmen in chain and shield, armed with spear and sword (50%) or composite bow and sword (50%), and other people and animals in proportion to the number of men.
  • Tactics: they usually withdraw from a force that inflicts over 25% casualties on them if the enemy seems able to keep up stout resistance. They also fake retreats to lure enemies into ambush. They are 75% likely to capture weaker groups, and 90% likely to parley with parties of near equal strength.

system.description:
Merchants trade in goods and merchandise, traveling in caravans (pack animals and/or wagons) from city to city to do business, so they are found almost everywhere. They always ride very swift, light horses.

  • Make-up: only 10% of a band are actual tradesmen and 10% drovers; the other 80% are mercenary guards.
  • Guard leaders: a fighter of 6th-11th level, with a lieutenant 1 level lower (5th-10th) and 12 guards of 2nd level.
  • Others: for every 50 persons in the caravan, a 10% chance of a magic-user of 6th-8th level, a 5% chance of a cleric of 5th-7th level, and a 15% chance of a thief of 8th-10th level with 1-4 lesser thieves (roll each one’s level, 3rd-7th).
  • All leaders, guards, and special characters are in addition to the number rolled.

Mercenary mounts, armor, and arms:

heavy warhorse, plate armor & shield, lance, sword*10%
medium warhorse, chainmail & shield, lance, sword20%
medium warhorse, chainmail & shield, flail, mace10%
light warhorse, scale mail, light crossbow, sword10%
chainmail, pole arm, mace10%
chainmail, heavy crossbow, mace10%
ringmail & shield, spear, morning star30%

* All 1st-level fighters.

All higher-level fighters and clerics have plate armor and shield.

Treasure: each merchant carries J, K, L, M, N, and Q; each mercenary type K, and leaders type M. Hidden somewhere in the caravan is the pay chest (100% certain), holding 2,000-4,000 gold pieces, 100-400 platinum pieces, and 4-16 gems of base 100 gold piece value. The merchandise is worth 10,000 to 60,000 gold pieces, carried by pack animals and/or wagons: 10 pack beasts or 1 wagon for each 5,000 gold pieces worth of goods.

system.description:
Pilgrims are simply groups traveling to some place holy (or unholy) to them, so they are found almost everywhere.

  • Clerics: a group always also has 1-6 2nd-level clerics, 1-4 4th-level clerics, 1-2 6th-level clerics, and 1 8th-level cleric with a 3rd-level and a 5th-level assistant.
  • Others: a 25% chance of a 5th- or 6th-level monk. For every 10 pilgrims, a 10% chance of 1-10 fighters of 1st-8th level, the same chance of 1-6 thieves of 2nd-7th level, and a 5% chance of a magic-user of 6th-9th level.
  • By alignment: lawful good pilgrims’ fighters are paladins; chaotic good ones’ fighters are rangers; neutral ones’ clerics are druids; lawful evil pilgrims all fight as berserkers, though armed only with daggers; chaotic evil ones’ thieves are assassins of the level rolled.
  • Psionics: all above-average characters have normal chances of psionic abilities.
  • Travel: 75% likely all on foot, 25% likely all mounted.

Alignment of a group:

lawful good35%
chaotic good20%
neutral10%
chaotic evil15%
lawful evil20%

Treasure: pilgrims and monks carry type J; fighters types L and M; clerics types J, K, and M; magic-users types L, N, and Q; thieves types J, N, and Q. There is a 5% chance that some high-level member carries a religious artifact, carefully hidden and well guarded by traps and/or magic devices.
