Mermen live in warm temperate and tropical seas and oceans, roaming to harvest sea plants and hunt fish; they even herd certain fish. They leave the water only to sun themselves or visit some coastal spot. They speak their own language, and 50% also speak locathah.

  • Communities: usually a reef or cliff honeycombed with passages and rooms; only 10% of the time do they build a village of shells, rocks, and coral. It has areas where the merwomen and young live (each 100% of the merman population), netted pens for food fish, workshops, and so on, and is guarded by 3-18 of the larger barracuda, which mermen have learned to tame.
  • Arms:
trident, dagger*50%
crossbow, dagger30%
net, javelin, dagger20%

* 20% of these also have grapples and 50’ lines.

Attacking ships: mermen sometimes attack surface vessels by surfacing and grappling them.

  • They throw grappling hooks up to 3” and are very accurate, 90% likely to hit.
  • 10 mermen then hold each line, and the ship is slowed 1” for each grapple. Meanwhile the other mermen shoot crossbows and darts at exposed crew.
  • If a hook is loosened or cut, the mermen pulling that line cannot attack in the next melee round.
  • They hold a ship motionless in 4-16 melee rounds; it then slowly sinks and is eventually looted.
  • During the attack they are exposed to missile fire from the ship, and take double damage from fire.

Mimics are underground creatures that cannot stand sunlight. They can imitate stone or wood perfectly, posing as stonework, doors, chests, or anything else they can copy. All mimics move about constantly looking for prey.

  • Two kinds: the large (9-10 dice), semi-intelligent, meat-eating “killer mimic”, which attacks anything nearby; and a slightly smaller intelligent kind, usually friendly if offered food.
  • Attack: when a creature touches a mimic, it lashes out with a pseudopod for 3-12 points of damage per hit, while oozing a glue that holds fast whatever part of the creature touched it.
  • Speech: killer mimics do not speak. The other kind has its own language and can usually speak several others, such as common, orcish, etc. For a consideration they usually tell a party what they have seen nearby.

Mind flayers are found only underground, since they detest sunlight. They are greatly evil and regard most of humanity (and its kin) as cattle to feed on.

  • Tentacles: it strikes with its four tentacles. A tentacle that hits reaches the victim’s brain in 1-4 melee rounds and draws it out, killing the creature at once; the mind flayer then eats the brain.
  • Mind blast: its more feared attack, a psionic blast in a cone 6” long, ½” across where it starts and 2” across at its far end. Everyone in it is affected (psionic attack on non-psionic).
  • Psionic powers: levitation, domination, ESP, body equilibrium, astral projection, and probability travel, at 7th level of mastery.
  • Cowardice: if an encounter goes against it, it flees at once to save itself, abandoning its fellows and its treasure.
  • Languages: only its own arcane language and several other weird tongues, said to be those of terrible races living far deeper underground than mankind has ever gone. They are also rumored to have a city somewhere deep beneath the earth.

Description: its skin glistens with slime and is a nauseous mauve, with purplish black tentacles. Its eyes are dead white with no visible pupil. Its hands are mauve, with three long reddish fingers each.

Minotaurs are usually found only in labyrinthine places in the wilderness or underground. They are cruel man-eaters; not particularly intelligent, but cunning, with excellent senses. They have their own language and are 25% likely to speak common too.

  • Hunting: they track prey by scent with 50% accuracy, always pursue prey in sight, and attack anything without fear unless it is clearly beyond their power to defeat.
  • Attacks: a butt against opponents 6’ or taller (2-8 points of damage), or a bite against shorter ones (1-4 points), plus a weapon, usually a huge axe (treat as a halberd) or a flail (+2 on damage).

Brown mold grows anywhere below ground, light tan to golden brown. It cannot stand strong ultraviolet light, but feeds on most other kinds of radiant energy. The temperature around a patch is below average.

  • Heat drain: it absorbs the body heat of any creature within 5’, even a basically cold-blooded one. Each melee round a creature is within 5’, the mold drains 1-8 hit points of frost damage for every 10 degrees of the creature’s body heat over 55 degrees.
  • Growth: worse, heat makes it grow instantly. A torch, flaming oil, or a fire ball near the patch lets it grow to 2, 4, or 8 times its area, so fast that on the next melee round it has spread and is draining heat in its new area.
  • Defenses: light spells and faerie fire do not feed it. Only magical cold affects it; no other magical or non-magical attack does. Ice storm or wall of ice makes it dormant for 5-30 turns. A cold wand or white dragon breath kills it.
  • It does not harm creatures that use cold (white dragons, ice toads, or winter wolves).

Yellow mold: a more common underground fungus, pale yellow to golden orange.

  • Enzymes: any creature that touches it is attacked by its enzymes. It also affects wood, more slowly, but does not harm metal or stone.
  • Spores: if touched roughly, there is a 50% chance per contact that the colony releases spores in a choking cloud 1” by 1” by 1”, centered where it was struck. Any creature in the cloud dies, its lungs filled with yellow mold, unless it saves versus poison. Saving such a victim takes a cure disease and a resurrection within 24 hours.
  • Defenses: only fire attacks affect it (flaming oil, a fire elemental, etc.). Continual light makes it dormant for 2-12 turns, but after that the mold grows over the light and blots it out.

Intelligent colonies: about 1 time in 6, a great colony of at least 300 square feet develops a collective intelligence, becoming mentally and psionically aware.

  • It attacks with spore clouds if it senses other life (sensing range 10’ to 60’), or psionically if psionic abilities are used within 20’ to 120’ (roll the sensing range randomly).
  • Psionically, it waits for the life form to come near, then launches an attack equal to the most powerful form of id insinuation. It can make 1 to 10 psionic attacks within as many turns, then must rest 1-4 days before it can attack this way again.
  • It cannot be attacked psionically in return unless a cleric able to communicate telepathically with plants is present to channel the attacks into a form that affects the colony’s plant intelligence. Otherwise it must be attacked and destroyed physically.

system.description:
The morkoth, or morlock, is a dim, shadowy monster often called the “wraith of the deep”, living in dark, deep waters. It may be humanoid, but reports vary.

  • Lair: a series of spiraling tunnels (typically 6), built so large creatures cannot enter, with the morkoth lurking where they meet. Their pattern is hypnotic: any creature passing over a tunnel is drawn toward it, and inside the passages approaches the morkoth without realizing it. The hypnotic effect is broken if the victim comes closer than 6”.
  • Charm: the morkoth then charms the victim with a spell unless it saves at −4, and devours it at leisure.
  • Bite: it attacks by biting; a charmed creature suffers this without knowing it, so the monster can eat it.
  • Spell reflection: it reflects spells of every kind back on the caster, possibly affecting others nearby with area spells. But if a dispel magic is cast at the same time, it cannot reflect the spell, and there is a 50% chance the magic affects it (it still gets a saving throw).

Mules are usually sterile crosses between horses and donkeys. Strong and agile, they can manage dungeons well in most cases. They can be very stubborn and uncooperative, and when contrary are likely to bite or kick their own handler. Fire does not panic them, but strange smells may make them bolt or start braying loudly. A mule can carry 2,000 gold pieces of weight at normal speed, or 6,000 at half speed.

Mummies are undead humans existing on both the normal and the positive material planes, found near their tombs or in similar burial places or ruins. Their evil keeps a semblance of life in them, and they seek to destroy every living thing they meet.

  • Blow: their unholy hatred of life and weird un-life give them tremendous power: a blow of the arm does 1-12 hit points of damage.
  • Rotting disease: every hit inflicts a disease, fatal in 1-6 months; each month it progresses, the victim permanently loses 2 points of charisma. Only the spell cure disease cures it. It negates all cure wound spells, and infected creatures heal at 10% of the normal rate.
  • Fear: merely seeing a mummy within 6” paralyzes any creature with fright and revulsion for 1-4 melee rounds, unless it saves versus magic. Numbers give courage: creatures get +1 on the save for each one beyond 6 per mummy. Humans facing a mummy save at +2.
  • Weapons: only magic weapons harm them, and those do only half damage, dropping fractions (5 becomes 2, 3 becomes 1, and 1 becomes 0).
  • Immunities: sleep, charm, hold, and cold-based spells have no effect, nor do poison and paralysis.
  • Raise dead: turns a mummy into a normal human (of 7th-level fighting ability, naturally) unless it saves versus magic.
  • Fire: even normal flame always damages them. A blow with a torch does 1-3 hit points; a flask of burning oil does 1-8 on the first round it covers the mummy and twice that on the second. Magical fire gets +1 per die of damage.
  • Holy water: 2-8 hit points of damage per vial that hits.
  • Victims: any creature killed by a mummy rots and cannot be raised unless cure disease and raise dead are both used within 6 turns.

Naga are snake-like creatures with good brains and magical abilities, found mostly in warm climates.

Guardian naga: wise and good, found mainly in sacred places, guarding treasure for lawful good followers, or watching over some evil.

  • Attacks: a poisonous bite (1-6 points of damage) and constriction (2-8 points).
  • Spit: poison at one creature up to 3” away; if the victim fails its saving throw versus poison, the spittle kills.
  • Spells: cleric spells as a 6th-level cleric: 2 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, 1 3rd-level, and 1 4th-level per day.
  • Appearance: green-gold scales with silvery triangles along the back, and golden eyes.

Spirit naga: totally evil, seeking to do harm whenever and wherever possible. They prefer ruined, dismal, or underground places.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-3 hit points of damage.
  • Gaze: permanently charms (as the spell) any humanoid that meets it, unless it saves versus paralyzation.
  • Spells: magic-user spells at 5th level and cleric spells at 4th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 1 3rd-level magic-user spells, and 2 1st-level and 1 2nd-level cleric spells per day.
  • Appearance: black scales with crimson bands; bulging heads that look very human, even to coloring and hair.

Water naga: found only in clear fresh water; curious but quite neutral, seldom attacking unless threatened or attacked first. Living far beneath the surface of a pool, lake, or river, they are seldom disturbed in their lair.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-4 points of damage.
  • Spells: magic-user spells (except those dealing with fire) at 5th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 2 3rd-level per day.
  • Appearance: emerald green to turquoise, in a net-like pattern with chocolate brown and pale jade green, or dark gray and olive. Eyes pale green to bright amber.

  • Spells: cleric spells as a 6th-level cleric: 2 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, 1 3rd-level, and 1 4th-level per day.
  • Appearance: green-gold scales with silvery triangles along the back, and golden eyes.

Spirit naga: totally evil, seeking to do harm whenever and wherever possible. They prefer ruined, dismal, or underground places.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-3 hit points of damage.
  • Gaze: permanently charms (as the spell) any humanoid that meets it, unless it saves versus paralyzation.
  • Spells: magic-user spells at 5th level and cleric spells at 4th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 1 3rd-level magic-user spells, and 2 1st-level and 1 2nd-level cleric spells per day.
  • Appearance: black scales with crimson bands; bulging heads that look very human, even to coloring and hair.

Water naga: found only in clear fresh water; curious but quite neutral, seldom attacking unless threatened or attacked first. Living far beneath the surface of a pool, lake, or river, they are seldom disturbed in their lair.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-4 points of damage.
  • Spells: magic-user spells (except those dealing with fire) at 5th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 2 3rd-level per day.
  • Appearance: emerald green to turquoise, in a net-like pattern with chocolate brown and pale jade green, or dark gray and olive. Eyes pale green to bright amber.

Naga are snake-like creatures with good brains and magical abilities, found mostly in warm climates.

Guardian naga: wise and good, found mainly in sacred places, guarding treasure for lawful good followers, or watching over some evil.

  • Attacks: a poisonous bite (1-6 points of damage) and constriction (2-8 points).
  • Spit: poison at one creature up to 3” away; if the victim fails its saving throw versus poison, the spittle kills.
  • Spells: cleric spells as a 6th-level cleric: 2 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, 1 3rd-level, and 1 4th-level per day.
  • Appearance: green-gold scales with silvery triangles along the back, and golden eyes.

Spirit naga: totally evil, seeking to do harm whenever and wherever possible. They prefer ruined, dismal, or underground places.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-3 hit points of damage.
  • Gaze: permanently charms (as the spell) any humanoid that meets it, unless it saves versus paralyzation.
  • Spells: magic-user spells at 5th level and cleric spells at 4th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 1 3rd-level magic-user spells, and 2 1st-level and 1 2nd-level cleric spells per day.
  • Appearance: black scales with crimson bands; bulging heads that look very human, even to coloring and hair.

Water naga: found only in clear fresh water; curious but quite neutral, seldom attacking unless threatened or attacked first. Living far beneath the surface of a pool, lake, or river, they are seldom disturbed in their lair.

  • Bite: poisonous, 1-4 points of damage.
  • Spells: magic-user spells (except those dealing with fire) at 5th level: 4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, and 2 3rd-level per day.
  • Appearance: emerald green to turquoise, in a net-like pattern with chocolate brown and pale jade green, or dark gray and olive. Eyes pale green to bright amber.

A larger, more intelligent species of otyugh. They share the otyugh’s general traits, but hunt prey even more aggressively and are slightly better at telepathic communication. Some reach 8’ across and 3’ or more high. Their hide is even tougher than an otyugh’s, though it looks similar.

The night hags rule the twisting planes of Hades and are seldom met elsewhere. There they are numerous, but on the material plane they appear only singly, always looking for very evil persons to slay and take to Hades to make another larva, a valuable commodity to demons and devils alike.

  • Sleep: when a night hag finds a very selfishly evil person, she casts a powerful sleep that affects even humans up to 12th level unless they save versus magic, then strangles the sleeping victim.
  • Riding: if the sleep fails, she visits the victim every night in ethereal form, invades his (or her) dreams to make the victim ethereal too, and rides the victim until dawn. The victim cannot get her off his back, and each night’s ride permanently drains one point of constitution. At 0 constitution the victim dies, and the hag returns to Hades with the larval soul.
  • Hatred: they hate goodness and attack any good creature whenever success looks likely.
  • Powers: magic missile 3 times per day (each missile doing 2-16 hit points), ray of enfeeblement 3 times per day, become ethereal at will, know alignment, and polymorph themselves at will.
  • Gating: if hard pressed, she can try to gate in a type I demon or a barbed devil (50%/50%), with a 50% chance the gate opens. She dislikes doing this, since she must then reward the demon or devil with a larva.
  • Defenses: completely immune to sleep, charm, fear, fire, and cold spells. Only silver, iron, or +3 or better weapons harm her.
  • Periapt: to project themselves astrally, night hags need a special periapt each forges in Hades. A hag whose periapt is taken cannot leave the plane she is on. The periapt cures diseases its holder catches and gives +2 on all saving throws, but in the hands of a good creature it decays 10% with each use, eventually vanishing.

Description: a hideous dark blue-violet, with black hair and glowing red eyes. Her taloned hands and feet have jet-black nails.

Also called “demon horses” and “hell horses”, nightmares come from the lower planes. The more powerful demons and devils ride them, as do night hags, and sometimes they carry undead such as spectres, vampires, and liches. They hate material life and attack viciously, even with no rider to command them.

  • Attacks: great fangs and burning hooves.
  • Smoke: in combat they breathe out a hot, smoking cloud that blinds and chokes; unless the opponent saves, it attacks at −2 on “to hit” and damage rolls.
  • Movement: they can fly, become ethereal, and roam the astral plane.

Description: gaunt and skeletal, with a huge head, glowing red eyes, flaming orange nostrils, and hooves that burn like embers. Its coat is dead black, and its mane and tail are wild and shaggy.

Nixies are water sprites living in lakes. They can go onto land but seldom do. They speak their own language and common.

  • Lair: dwellings woven of living seaweed, 95% unlikely to be noticed from any distance under 2”. Giant fish guard it, obeying simple commands: 1-2 gar (20%) or 2-5 pike (80%). Nixies can also summon 10-100 small fish.
  • Charm: nixies love enslaving humans. If humans come within 30’ of a group of nixies, the nixies produce a powerful charm, one per 10 nixies, which the victim must save against at −2. A dispel magic cast on a charmed person before he enters the water has a 75% chance of breaking it, but only 10% once he is in the water.
  • Enslavement: a charmed human is kept in their lair for 1 full year, after which the charm wears off and he may go free. During that time they keep water breathing on him. Each nixie can cast water breathing (lasting 1 day) on any creature, or dispel it, once per day.
  • Weapons: each carries a long dagger and a dart (javelin). The javelin is used as a spear underwater and thrown above it, up to 6” (1” short range, 3” medium, etc.).
  • Weaknesses: 25% magic resistant, but they fear fire and very bright light. A flaming sword or a light spell keeps them back. Continual light keeps them away until they can dim it by summoning small fish to crowd around it.

Description: very comely humanoids with greenish skin, dark green hair, and silver eyes. Their skin is lightly scaled, and their hands and feet webbed.

These beautiful women, who never seem to age, live in the loveliest wilderness places: grottos in the sea, clear lakes and streams, and crystalline caverns. They dislike any intrusion and have ways to prevent it. They speak their own language and common.

  • Powers: dimension door once per day, and druid spells at 7th level (4 1st-level, 2 2nd-level, 2 3rd-level, and 1 4th-level spell, each once per day).
  • Beauty: looking at a nymph causes permanent blindness unless the onlooker saves versus magic. If she is nude or undresses, an onlooker dies unless he saves versus magic.
  • Friendship: 10% chance she is friendly to a good creature that approaches without first glimpsing her (for example, by calling out or other advance notice). If she sees a good human male with 18 charisma before he sees her, she is 90% likely to be favorably inclined toward him.

Ochre jellies are a kind of giant amoeba that seep about dungeons hunting flesh or cellulose to eat, much preferring flesh. Their shapeless form lets them flow through small spaces and travel easily along walls or ceilings.

  • Attack: the fluids they ooze dissolve flesh (3-12 hit points per round of exposure).
  • Lightning: only divides it into one or more smaller jellies, each doing half normal damage.
  • “Cold and attacks have normal effect” (as printed).

Giant octopi live in warm waters of middle to shallow depth, lairing in wrecked ships and undersea caves. They hunt at night, snatching and eating any vulnerable life. Malicious and cunning, they readily attack swimmers or seize small boats to eat the crew, and several will cooperate to overwhelm a larger ship if they can. A vessel grabbed by giant octopi loses way and comes to a full stop in 3 turns.

  • Tentacles: it usually attacks with 6 of its 8 tentacles, using 2 to anchor itself. Each tentacle hit does only 1-4 hit points, but unless loosened or cut off, it does twice that (2-8 points) every melee round after.
  • Beak: a vicious beak bites nearby prey for 2-12 hit points.
  • Grip: a creature is struck by only 1 tentacle at a time unless it is larger than about 8’ tall or long. There is a 25% chance that a creature struck has both upper limbs pinned, and a 25% chance that neither is held. With both held it cannot attack with them; with only 1 pinned it attacks at −3 to hit; with both free, at only −1. A tentacle grips with 18/20 strength. A creature of 18/20 strength or more can grab the tentacle and stop its squeezing, but that does not free it, and the octopus at once tries to drag the victim to its mouth to eat it.
  • Breaking free: a tentacle must be cut off. Each takes 8 hit points, in addition to the octopus’s own 8 dice.
  • Retreat: if 3 or more tentacles are cut off, it is 90% likely to retreat, squirting a cloud of black ink 4” high by 6” wide by 6” long that completely blocks the vision of anything inside it. It then flees to its lair or hides somewhere nearby, changing color to blend with its surroundings.

system.treasure: Individuals M (× 10), Q, B, S in lair
system.description:
Ogres are found in almost any terrain, including underground. They are ugly-tempered and voracious, and fond of treasure. They sometimes serve as mercenaries for orc tribes or evil clerics, or join gnolls for a profitable raid. They mix freely with trolls and some giants, and certain demons sometimes enslave them. They speak their own language and those of chaotic evil, orcs, trolls, and stone giants.

  • Leaders: with 11 or more ogres, one is a leader (armor class 3, 30-33 hit points, attacks as a 7 hit dice creature, 2-12 hit points damage per attack). With 16 or more, there are 2 such leaders plus a chieftain (armor class 4, 34-37 hit points, attacks as a 7 hit dice monster, 4-14 hit points damage per attack).
  • Weapon damage: if damage is figured by weapon type, give ogres a standard +2 hit points, and leaders/chieftains an extra +1/+2.
  • Lair: 2-12 females (fight as normal ogres, but do only 2-8 points of damage and have at most 6 hit points per hit die) and 2-8 young (fight as goblins).
  • Prisoners: they take prisoners as slaves (25%) or food (75%), so there is a 30% chance of 2-8 slaves/prisoners in the lair. They are very fond of halfling, dwarf, or elf flesh, so there is only a 10% chance of finding such creatures alive there.

Description: hide from dull blackish-brown to dead yellow; rare ones are sickly violet. Their warty bumps are often a different color, or at least darker. Hair blackish-blue to dull dark green; eyes purple with white pupils; teeth and talons black or orange. They wear any kind of skins or furs and keep their arms and armor reasonably well. They live at least 90 years.

Japanese ogres (ogre magi) are not as rare elsewhere as they are here. They usually seek uninhabited places to lair, typically a fortified dwelling or a secure underground cavern complex, from which they raid for treasure and for humans as slaves and food. They speak their own language, that of normal ogres, common, and their alignment tongue.

  • Lair: always a chief of great strength (+2 on each hit die, attacking and saving as a 9 hit dice monster) besides the others rolled, and 2-12 slaves/prisoners.
  • At will: fly (for 12 turns), invisibility, darkness in a 1” radius, polymorph into human (or a similar two-legged humanoid form 4’ to 12’ tall), and regenerate 1 hit point per melee round (lost parts must be reattached to regenerate).
  • Once per day each: charm person, sleep, assume gaseous form, and a ray of cold the size of a cold wand’s, doing 8 eight-sided dice of damage (unless the appropriate saving throw is made).

Description: light blue, light green, or pale brown skin, with hair usually of a contrasting, darker color (blue-green, green-blue), except that brown-skinned ones have dark yellow hair. Black nails, very white teeth and tusks, ivory horns, and eyes with dark pupils and white centers. Their clothing is usually patterned in the styles of their homeland.

system.treasure: Individuals L; C, O, Q (× 10), S in lair
system.description:
Orc tribes are fiercely competitive: when two meet, they are 75% likely to fight each other unless a strong leader (such as a wizard, evil priest, or evil lord) with enough force behind him is there to control them. Being bullies, the stronger always intimidate and dominate the weaker (if goblins are near and the orcs are strong enough, for example, they happily bully them). Orcs hate light and live where sunlight is dim or absent. In full daylight they subtract 1 from their rolls to hit, but they see well even in total darkness (infravision).

Tribes: known tribes include the Vile Rune, Bloody Head, Death Moon, Broken Bone, Evil Eye, Leprous Hand, Rotting Eye, and Dripping Blade. If orcs of one of these tribes are met in an area, all other orcs nearby are likely to be of the same tribe.

  • Leaders: for every 30 orcs, a leader and 3 assistants, with 8 hit points each (the biggest, strongest, meanest of their group). With 150 or more, also a sub-chief and 3-18 guards (armor class 4, 11 hit points, fight as 2 hit dice monsters, 2-7 hit points damage).
  • Supply trains: orcs met away from their lair have a 20% chance of escorting a train of 1-6 carts and 10-60 slave bearers, carrying supplies and loot to their chief or a stronger tribe. Each cart holds goods worth 10 to 1,000 gold pieces, and each slave carries goods worth 5 to 30. With a train, double the leaders and assistants, add 10 normal orcs per cart, and a sub-chief with 5-30 guards is always in charge.
  • Lair: underground 75% of the time, an above-ground village 25%. It always holds a chief and 5-30 bodyguards (AC 4, 13-16 hit points, attack as 3 hit dice monsters, 2-8 hit points damage), females equal to 50% of the males, and young equal to 100%. Underground, there is a 50% chance of 2-5 ogres living with them. Above ground, it is a crude village of wooden huts protected by a ditch, rampart, and log palisade, with 1-4 watch towers and a single gate, and 1 catapult and 1 ballista per 100 male orcs (round to the nearest hundred).
  • Weapons: typically:
sword & flail5%
sword & spear10%
axe & spear10%
axe & pole arm10%
axe & crossbow10%
axe & bow10%
sword & battleaxe5%
spear10%
axe10%
polearm20%
  • Leaders and above always carry two weapons.
  • Standard: with a sub-chief, the tribal standard is present 40% of the time, and always when the chief is. All orcs within 6” of it fight more fiercely (+1 on hit dice and morale check dice).
  • Nature: cruel, hating living things in general and elves above all, whom they always attack first. They take slaves for work, food, and entertainment (torture, etc.), but kill elves at once.
  • Mining: accomplished tunnelers and miners; they notice new or unusual construction underground 35% of the time and sloping passages 25%.
  • Languages: most speak goblin, hobgoblin, and ogre, besides orc and lawful evil.

Description: particularly disgusting, since their brown or brownish green coloring with a bluish sheen sets off their pinkish snouts and ears. Their bristly hair is dark brown or black, sometimes with tan patches. Even their armor tends to be ugly, dirty and often a bit rusty. They favor unpleasant colors generally; their clothing, shield devices, and trim are in tribal colors such as blood red, rust red, mustard yellow, yellow green, moss green, greenish purple, and blackish brown. They live 40 years.

Half-orcs: orcs breed with anything, so there are many unsavory mongrels with orcish blood, particularly orc-goblins, orc-hobgoblins, and orc-humans. Orcs cannot interbreed with elves. Half-orcs strongly favor the orcish side, so they are basically orcs, though sometimes (10%) they can pass as true members of their other stock (goblins, hobgoblins, humans, etc.).

Giant otters live in lakes and rivers. They are basically not aggressive, but fight fiercely if threatened or cornered. They love to play, and sliding and tag are favorite games. If met while playing, they may panic horses, overturn wagons, accidentally break carts, etc. In water they may likewise accidentally overturn boats and other small craft in their playfulness.

  • Lair: always 5 giant otters: 2 adults and 3 young (40%-70% grown). The parents always attack in this case, and the young defend themselves.
  • Pelts: sell for 1,000 to 4,000 gold pieces.

These weird monsters are scavengers that eat almost anything, quite willing to add some fresh meat to their diet of dung, offal, and carrion. They hate direct sunlight or bright light, so they are usually found underground. Usually (90%) only one is met, since otyugh typically live in partnership with other underground monsters, keeping a truce with powerful monsters so they can scavenge droppings and other leavings. Most live in piles of dung and rubbish, and thrive there.

  • Body: a sensory stalk and two tentacle arms stick out of its hideous body. Its eyes are always raised above the offal it lies under, so it cannot be surprised.
  • Attacks: its tentacles have sharp ridges and deliver smashing blows. Its sucker-like mouth is full of teeth, and any victim it bites is 90% likely to be infected with disease (typhus).
  • Treasure: it has no interest in treasure as humans know it, but its partners may, sometimes requiring it to guard treasure they value as a condition of letting it live with them in semi-symbiosis.
  • Speech: its own language, and it is semi-telepathic, so it can often communicate with other life forms when it wishes.

(See also NEO-OTYUGH.)

Giant owls are rarely met, since they live only in very wild areas. They are night-hunting predators and effective hunters, and speak their own language.

  • Attacks: two sets of sharp talons and a strong beak.
  • Silence: their feathers let them fly almost silently, so they surprise on 1-5 (on d6).
  • Friendship: they are intelligent and sometimes befriend other creatures.
  • Lair: 20% chance of 1-3 eggs (25%) or 1-3 young owls (20% to 70% grown). The parents always attack any creature threatening the eggs or young. Eggs sell for 1,000 gold pieces and young for 2,000 on the open market.

The horrible owlbear is probably the result of an insane wizard’s breeding experiments. It lives in tangled forests of every temperate climate and in underground labyrinths. Ravenous, aggressive, and always evil-tempered, it attacks prey on sight and fights to the death.

  • Attacks: great claws (two inches long on large males) and a snapping beak; then it seizes a victim and squeezes and bites it to death.
  • Hug: if either forepaw hits with a roll of 18 or better, the owlbear has dragged the victim to it, and the victim takes an extra 2-16 hit points of damage from the hug that melee round and every round after until the owlbear is killed. (If an 18 would not hit the opponent’s armor class, the hug does not work and does no damage.)
  • Lair: 25% chance of 1-6 eggs (20%) or young (80%) besides the adults. Young are 40% to 70% grown and fight accordingly. Eggs are worth 2,000 gold pieces, and young under 50% grown 5,000, on the open market.

Description: fur and feathers brownish-black to yellow brown; the males (1,300 to 1,500 pounds) are darker. Beaks yellow to ivory. The red-rimmed eyes are exceedingly terrible to see.

Pegasi live in remote places, being usually very shy and wild. These intelligent winged horses are the swiftest of steeds and much sought after for that reason. They serve only good characters, but those they serve, they serve to the death.

  • Attacks: two front hooves and powerful teeth.
  • Carrying: a male carries as much as a medium warhorse; a female as much as a light warhorse.
  • Lair: 1 nest per pair, with a 20% chance per nest of 1-2 eggs (30%) or young (70%) of 20% to 50% maturity. Eggs are worth 3,000 gold pieces and young 5,000 on the open market.

Perytons live in rocky hills or mountains. They eat both plants and meat, and look very weird, probably the result of the same kind of experiment that produced the owlbear. They speak their own language.

  • Attack: its sharp horns, at +2 to hit; its claws are too weak to use. Each peryton attacks only one creature. When it is dead, the peryton tears out its heart with its teeth and flies away at once, since it needs the heart to reproduce. Human hearts are the kind it wants most.
  • Defense: normal weapons do not harm it.
  • Lair: caves high on cliffs or mountain peaks. They sometimes take humans and similar creatures alive and keep them prisoner until needed for food or reproduction.

Description: blue-black upper body and head, with jet-black horns. Wing and back feathers are dark green; the male’s chest is light to medium blue, while females are drab.

Piercers live in caves, caverns, and similar underground places. Their stony outer casing makes them look exactly like stalactites on a cave roof. Noise and heat draw them, and when a living creature passes beneath, they drop on it to kill and eat it. Larger ones are found with smaller ones.

Size: equal to its hit dice, with an equal chance of 1, 2, 3, or 4 dice. The largest is about 6’ long, 1’ across at the base, and weighs 500 pounds.
system.hpNote: Equal chance of 1, 2, 3 or 4 hit dice; size equals hit dice (MM p.78).

system.description: Giant pike live in large, deep lakes. These aggressive predators readily attack any nearby creature when hungry. They see well and move very fast, surprising prey two-thirds of the time. Nixies often tame them.

Pixies live only in the most idyllic woodlands. They are naturally invisible, so they are almost never noticed even when some creature passes near their secluded home. They are highly mischievous and likely to bother, harass, or fool creatures. They speak their own tongue, that of sprites, and common.

  • Weapons: slim swords (equal to daggers) and fine bows like those of sprites. Their arrows are more effective, all at +4 to hit, of three kinds: war arrows doing 2-5 hit points of damage; sleep arrows that put any creature struck into a comatose sleep for 1-6 hours unless it saves versus magic; and memory arrows that do no physical harm, but cause complete loss of memory, restorable only by clerical exorcism, unless the victim saves versus magic.
  • At will: become visible, polymorph themselves, and know alignment.
  • Once per day each: create illusions with sound and sight that last without concentration until magically dispelled, dispel magic (at 8th level), dancing lights, and ESP; 1 in 10 can also use irresistible dance.
  • Confusion: their touch causes confusion in any creature that fails a saving throw versus magic. It is permanent unless remove curse is applied.
  • Invisibility: opponents unable to detect invisible objects subtract 4 from their “to hit” rolls, and pixies can attack while invisible.

Giant porcupines are found mainly in wooded areas. They are stupid and not aggressive, but defend themselves easily when threatened. A giant porcupine treats any approach within 30’ as a threat.

  • Quills: its main defense is to shoot 1-8 quills from its tail, each doing 1-4 hit points of damage, with a range of 30’. Its quills are up to 3’ long, so any attack from within 6’ also suffers 1-4 quills in return from its defensive movements. There is no practical limit to its quills: over 80 in its tail and over 300 on its body.
  • Bite: it can bite with some effect, but only in the most desperate defense (10% chance per melee round once it has taken over 50% damage).

Portuguese men-o-war float in warm seas, trailing deadly tentacles below. Any creature touching the tentacles takes damage from their poison, and unless it saves versus paralyzation, it is paralyzed, drawn up by the tentacles, and devoured in 3-12 turns.

  • Tentacles: 10-40, with 10’ of length per hit die. A one hit die man-o-war is 2½’ across with 10 tentacles 10’ long; two hit dice, 20 tentacles 20’ long; three hit dice, 30 tentacles 30’ long; four hit dice, 10’ across with 40 tentacles trailing 40’ down.
  • Severing: each tentacle takes only a single hit point to cut off, but that does not damage the creature, and tentacles regrow in several days. Only hits on the body can kill it.
  • Transparent: 90% likely to go unnoticed unless the creature meeting it can detect invisible objects.
system.hpNote: 10’ of tentacle per hit die; a tentacle takes 1 hit point to cut off but this does not harm the creature (MM p.79).

system.description:
Pseudo-dragons live in any climate except the coldest or hottest, when they are found at all; they are rare indeed and highly sought after. They lair in great hollow trees or small caves.

  • Attacks: a vicious bite with small dragon-like jaws, but their main weapon is a long, very flexible stinging tail that moves with flashing speed, striking at +4 to hit. A creature stung must save versus poison or fall into catalepsy for 1-6 days, appearing dead, with a 25% chance of actually dying.
  • Camouflage: a chameleon-like power lets them blend into any typical background, becoming 80% undetectable to creatures unable to see invisible objects. They can themselves see invisible objects.
  • Magic resistance: innate, and they can share it with a human (or humanoid) companion they are touching.
  • Telepathy: they communicate by a limited telepathy. One that chooses to become a human’s (or humanoid’s) companion can also send what it sees and hears to its companion up to 24” away.

Description: exactly like miniature red dragons, but basically red brown in color, which they can change as described above.

Purple worms burrow deep underground, constantly searching for food. They sense vibrations at 60’ and move to attack. Usually only adults are met, 8’-9’ across and 40’-50’ long. Young are 1’ across and about 5’ long when they hatch, 10-20 per hatching, each with 1 hit die +4 hit points. Worms return to their lairs to rest, and there expel indigestible waste such as metal and mineral crystals.

  • Bite: 2-24 points of damage. A hit 20% over the score needed (that is, 4 or more over the required number), or any roll of 20 (100%), means it has swallowed its victim whole. A mature worm can swallow a creature about 8’ tall and up to 6’ wide, or the reverse.
  • Swallowed: a swallowed creature dies in 6 melee rounds, and the worm digests it in 12 turns, after which it is completely gone and cannot be raised. The creature can try to cut its way out: the worm’s inner armor class is 9, but each round inside, the creature subtracts 1 from the damage of each of its attacks, cumulatively (−2 on the second melee round, −3 on the third, etc.).
  • Sting: a poisonous stinger in its tail, used only to defend its rear, or when fighting large or numerous opponents in a very spacious area that leaves room to use it. It does 2-8 hit points of damage, and a victim that fails its poison saving throw is killed.

Mottled worm: an aquatic purple worm that lives in shallow bottom muck but surfaces for prey. Otherwise like the purple worm.

Quasits are rare on the material plane but not on the planes of Pandemonium and the Abyss. A quasit is a larva changed into a minor demon to serve as familiar to a chaotic evil magic-user or cleric. Its intelligence is low, but it is sly and cunning, and in certain situations can call on the thinking power of a demon lord.

  • Forms: its demon lord gives it the power to polymorph into any two of: giant centipede, bat, frog, or wolf. It keeps its magical powers in its polymorphed forms.
  • Attacks: in its own form, claws and fangs. Claw wounds cause a burning itch that drains 1 point of dexterity per wound unless the victim saves versus poison; the loss lasts 2-12 melee rounds.
  • Powers: all quasits detect good and detect magic, regenerate 1 hit point per melee round, and become invisible at will. Once per day they can send out a blast of fear in a 3” radius.
  • Defenses: only magic or cold iron weapons harm them; cold, fire, and lightning do not affect them. Against spells they count as 7 hit dice creatures.

As a familiar, it gives its “master”:

  • telepathic communication, letting the master use all its senses (including infravision), up to a mile away;
  • within 1”: the quasit’s magic resistance (25%) and regeneration of 1 hit point per melee round;
  • within a mile: one extra level of ability; farther away, the master loses 1 level, and if the quasit is killed, 4 levels;
  • besides its normal advice, once per week it can contact a lower plane to help its master decide a course of action, like a commune spell but with 6 questions.

Aims: its main goal is to help its master work greater and more chaotic evil. It also wants to destroy lawful evil humans to steal their souls for the demons, since it will be rewarded for them when (and if) it returns to the Abyss. When its master dies, it must seize the soul and rush back there. If it has not been actively evil before then, its demon lord might change it into a manes or larva, or send it out as a quasit again, rather than making it a type I or II demon.

First known in India, these evil spirits in flesh are spreading. They like to eat human meat, and as masters of illusion they easily get it. If more than 1 is met in its lair, the group is a male and 1 or more females.

  • Deception: they use ESP, then create an illusion of whatever those they meet consider friendly, holding back their attack until they can catch their prey off guard.
  • Spells: they can use magic-user spells (up to 3rd level) and cleric spells (1st level).
  • Defenses: spells under 8th level do not affect them. Non-magical weapons cannot harm them, and magic weapons below +3 do half damage. But a hit by a crossbow bolt blessed by a cleric kills them.

Giant sheep are found only in hilly or mountainous regions. All full-grown ones, male or female, have the statistics above, but males (giant rams) charge to attack, butting for double the damage shown. They are not normally aggressive, but defend the flock to the death if they think it is threatened.

A flock is a ram, four ewes, and lambs for the rest (roll percentile dice for size, halve the number rolled, and add it to 50%).

Rats of all sorts are common, and giant Sumatran rats are a plague in many places such as crypts and dungeons. Their burrows honeycomb many graveyards, where they try to cheat ghouls of their prizes by tunneling to newly buried corpses.

  • Disease: each wound from a giant rat’s bite has a 5% chance of passing on a serious disease; if so, the victim is diseased unless he saves versus poison.
  • Behavior: they avoid attacking strong parties unless commanded to fight by creatures such as wererats or vampires. They fear fire and flee from it. They swim quite well and can attack in water.

Manta ray: these huge creatures “fly” through warm ocean waters looking for prey. Small ones measure 32’ from tip to tip, and the largest grow to about 44’ across. They often rest on the sea floor, their color blending with the bottom, waiting for a victim to pass, and then attack.

  • Swallowing: its huge mouth, one-quarter of its width, can engulf most non-giant creatures in one gulp. If it rolls 10% (2 numbers) over the score it needs to hit, it has swallowed any prey that fits in its mouth. A swallowed creature dies in 6 melee rounds. It can attack the ray from inside (its armor class is the same), but with a cumulative −1 per melee round on damage, so −6 in the last round before it dies.
  • Tail spine: 2-20 points of damage to any creature it strikes, and the victim is stunned for 2-8 melee rounds by the force of the blow unless it saves against paralyzation. The ray uses its tail only when seriously threatened, and only against an opponent at its rear quarter.
  • Treasure: its stomach holds indigestible items, such as the treasure types listed.

Pungi ray: another tropical ray, found only on fairly shallow bottoms. It hides in the sand with its terrible back spines sticking out. The spines are greenish or brown and so like plant growth that they are 90% indistinguishable from normal seaweed.

  • Size: about 15’ across and 6’ or so long. The spines cover an area 3’ by 4’, averaging 1 per square foot (12 in all), and are 1’ to 2’ long.
  • Spines: any creature landing on a spine must save versus poison or be killed instantly. A footstep on a pungi ray is 1 attack; a human falling across one suffers 2-8 spine attacks.
  • If attacked, it tries to escape by fleeing.

Sting ray: seemingly harmless bottom feeders of shallow tropical waters, but they cover themselves with sand and are 90% invisible. Any creature that steps on one is lashed by its tail spine for 1-3 points of damage on a hit, and must save versus poison or be paralyzed for 5-20 turns, taking that many extra hit points of damage.

Remorhaz, sometimes called polar worms, live only in the chill wastes and are very aggressive predators.

  • Size: set by hit dice: 7 dice is 21’ long, 8 dice 24’ long, etc.
  • Lair: 25% chance of a mate and 1-2 eggs. Eggs are worth 5,000 gold pieces each.
  • Attack: it beats its small wings, rears up the front of its body, and snaps forward with blinding speed. The largest can swallow prey whole this way, on a roll of 20; a swallowed victim is killed instantly by the intense heat of its digestive system.
  • Heat: when roused, it secretes substances that make its insides very hot, and the protrusions on its back glow cherry-red. Any non-magical weapon striking its back melts, and any creature touching those surfaces takes 10-100 points of damage.

Description: ice blue all over except along its back, where a white streak sets off the large protrusions. Its many-faceted eyes are white.

Rhinoceroses are mostly aggressive plant-eaters. A few kinds are less aggressive and run if they feel threatened, but most charge. They see poorly but have keen hearing and smell.

  • Young: if more than half the possible number are met, 1 or 2 are young (30% to 60% grown).
  • Kinds: one-horned rhinos have 8 hit dice and do 2-8 hit points of damage; two-horned rhinos have 9 hit dice and do more (2-12 points).
  • Charge: double damage.
  • Trampling: they trample any opponent low enough, doing 2-8 hit points of damage for each forefoot that hits.

Woolly rhinoceros: a large, very aggressive species roaming the cold temperate and subarctic regions of the Pleistocene epoch, otherwise like its modern relatives.

  • Charge: double damage.
  • Trampling: they trample any opponent low enough, doing 2-8 hit points of damage for each forefoot that hits.

Rocs are huge birds somewhat like eagles, living in the highest mountains of warm regions. They prey on large creatures such as cattle, horses, and elephants, swooping down, seizing the prey in their powerful talons, and carrying it off to their lair. If the creature resists, the roc strikes it with its beak for 4-24 points of damage per hit. Its lair is a vast nest of trees, branches, and the like, with treasure strewn about; the roc does not value it, since it is only what is left of its victims. Giants sometimes tame and use rocs.

Ropers live in underground caverns. They prey on all kinds of creatures, but humans are their favorite food. A roper can stand upright to look like a pillar or stalagmite, or lie flat on the floor so it looks like nothing but a hump.

  • Strands: it can shoot six strands of a strong, sticky, rope-like substance 2”-5”. A hit causes weakness (50% of strength lost in 1-3 melee rounds), and the roper then draws its prey into its toothy mouth to be quickly devoured. The chance of breaking a strand is the same as for opening a door, but each round the roper drags the victim 10’ closer.
  • Defenses: lightning does not affect it, and cold does half damage at most, but it is very vulnerable to fire (−4 on its saving throw).
  • Gizzard: holds 3-18 platinum pieces, and has a 35% chance of 5-20 gems.

Description: a yellowish gray mass that looks like foul, festering corruption, cigar-shaped, about 9’ long and some 3’ across.

Rot grubs are sometimes found in heaps of offal or dung, and rarely in ceilings, walls, or floors. These small creatures greatly enjoy living flesh, and viciously burrow into any that touches them. The victim must at once put flame to the wound (1-6 hit points of damage per application) or have cure disease cast on him. Otherwise the grubs burrow to the heart and kill their host in 1-3 turns.

Rust monsters live only in dark underground places, roaming in search of their food: metal of all kinds, but mainly ferrous metals such as iron, steel, and steel alloys (such as mithral and adamantite arms and armor).

  • Antennae: if it touches metal with its two antennae (roll to hit), the metal rusts or corrodes and at once falls to pieces, which the creature easily eats and digests.
  • Magic items: get a saving throw: a 10% chance per plus of not being affected (a +2 weapon or armor has a 20% chance).
  • Weapons: any weapon striking a rust monster is affected just as if its antennae had touched it.
  • Distraction: it smells metal 9” away. It stops for a melee round to eat things such as a handful of iron spikes or a mace if a fleeing party throws them down, and prefers ferrous metal to copper, silver, etc.

system.treasure: Individuals N; I, O, P, Q (× 10), X, Y in lair
system.description:
The sahuagin, sometimes called “sea devils” or “devil men of the deep”, live in warm salt waters 100’ to 1,500’ deep. They are predatory in the extreme and a constant threat to all living things, killing for sport and pleasure as well as food. They loathe fresh water and dislike light, and bright light (such as a light spell) hurts their eyes. On dark, moonless nights they come ashore to raid and plunder human villages. They hate even the evil ixitxachitl; only sharks are their friends. They speak their own tongue, and some can apparently talk with the ixitxachitl in theirs.

Society: a king rules them from a vast undersea city deep beneath the waves. His realm is divided into 9 provinces, each ruled by a prince who controls the small groups of sahuagin in his fief. This mirrors the planes of Hell, since sahuagin worship devils.

  • Bands: always led by a chieftain (4 hit dice +4 hit points) with 1 lieutenant (3 hit dice +3 hit points) for every 10 members, in addition to the group.
  • Lair: also 1 baron (6 hit dice + 6 hit points), 9 guards (3 hit dice + 3 hit points), 30-120 females (2 hit dice), 10-40 hatchlings (1 hit die), and 20-80 eggs, plus 2-8 sharks that obey simple one- or two-word commands.
  • Clerics: females dominate their religious life. There is a 10% chance per 10 males of an (evil) cleric of 5th to 8th level with 1-4 assistant priestesses of 3rd or 4th level.
  • Prince’s stronghold: any lair has a 5% chance of being one. The prince has 8 hit dice +8 hit points and 9 guards of chieftain strength, with 1 8th-level evil high priestess and 4 4th-level under-clerics. Males, females, hatchlings, and eggs are double the number rolled, and 4-24 sharks are always present.
  • Buildings: lairs are true villages or towns of domed stone buildings, hard to spot under the seaweed and similar plants growing on and around them.

Arms: they wear no armor, but their scaly hides are very tough, equal to armor class 5. They wear harnesses for their gear and weapons. A group is typically armed:

spear & dagger30%
trident, net & dagger50%
heavy crossbow & dagger20%
  • Spears are used only for thrusting.
  • Nets are set with dozens of hooks, making escape virtually impossible for unarmored victims or creatures unable to grip and tear with 16 or more strength. They are used to trap victims, and are replaced by 3 javelins when a band raids on land.
  • Crossbows shoot at most 30’ underwater, and normally above water.
  • Tridents have three uses: to spear small prey, to pin prey trapped in nets, and to hold threatening opponents at bay.

Unarmed: long, sharp claws on their webbed hands do 1-2 hit points each, and both can be used at once. Their powerful taloned rear legs kick for 1-4 hit points with each foot that hits. Their mouths are full of teeth and fangs, biting for 1-4 points. So an unarmed sahuagin can attack 3 or 5 times per melee round: 1-2/1-2/1-4, plus 1-4/1-4 if the legs can rake.

Senses: very keen. They see 30” underwater at 100’ depth, 1” less for each further 100’ (26” at 500’, 21” at 1,000’). They hear the clink of metal, or an oar splashing, 1 mile away. But within 24” they cannot hear swimming or similar noise, though they still hear metallic or other clanks, clicks, thuds, etc.

Description: typically blackish green on the back, shading to green on the belly, with black fins and great, staring, deep shining black eyes. About 1 in 216 is a mutant with 4 fully usable arms, usually black shading to gray. Females look like males but slightly smaller. Hatchlings are light-colored, darkening and reaching full growth about 1-2 months after hatching.

History and legend: the sahuagin are recorded because of their evil: again and again they have raided the land, laying waste whole coasts, and they constantly destroy passing ships. Their origin is unknown. Some suggest the most powerful lawful evil gods made them from a nation of especially evil humans to preserve them when the deluge came on the earth. The tritons, however, are said to claim that sahuagin are distant relatives of the sea elves, spawned by the drow.

  • Prisoners: few survive capture. Captives are taken to the lair and kept in cells. Sahuagin can stay out of water up to 4 hours, but a typical village has no air in its cells; only the nobles’ towns have special quarters for air-breathers. A few prisoners are set aside for torture and sport, typically a fight to the death between two different creatures in an arena; the rest are simply killed and eaten. Prisoners seldom escape, though the sahuagin enjoy letting captives think they are free, only to surround them with sadistic guards while a school of sharks comes for the kill.
  • Strength: they are cruel and brutal, the strongest always bullying the weaker. These cannibals kill and eat any injured, disabled, or infirm sahuagin, even imperfect hatchlings. This harsh law has bred a strong race, and any leader can always be challenged. Challenge duels are fought without weapons (only fang and claw), and the loser is always slain, in the fight or afterward.
  • Growth: sahuagin never stop growing, though slowly, and most die before living long enough to grow large. Leaders are the largest and strongest. The 9 princes, and the king, are each said to be of the 4-armed kind.
  • The king: said to live in a city at the greatest depth sahuagin can survive, built along both walls of an undersea canyon, home to fully 5,000 sahuagin besides the king’s retinue of queens, concubines, nobles, guards, etc. (said to number 1,000 or more). The king is reported to be huge (10 hit dice + 10 hit points) and of the greatest evil, always with 9 noble guards (6 hit dice + 6 hit points) and the evil high priestess of all sahuagin with her train of 9 under-clerics.

Salamanders are creatures of the elemental plane of fire that sometimes come to the material plane for reasons known only to them. They hate cold, preferring temperatures of 300 degrees and up, and can stand lower temperatures for only a few hours. Their lair is usually at least 500 degrees, so any treasure there is the kind that survives such heat.

  • Armor: the human-like upper body is armor class 5; the lower body armor class 3.
  • Attacks: usually a metal spear doing 1-6 hit points plus 1-6 more for its heat. At the same time it can lash its snake-like tail around an opponent, squeezing for 2-12 hit points plus 1-6 from its body heat. Fire-resistant creatures take no heat damage but still take normal attack damage.
  • Defenses: only magic weapons, or creatures of a magical nature or great strength, can affect it. It is immune to all fire attacks, and sleep, charm, and hold spells do not work on it. Cold attacks do 1 extra point of damage per die.

Description: copper-colored head and torso with glowing yellow eyes; the lower body is orange, shading to dull red at the tail.

Satyrs (or fauns) live only in sylvan woodlands, caring mainly for sport: frolicking, piping, chasing wood nymphs, etc. They resent intrusion and drive away any creature that offends them, though they can sometimes be lured or bribed with superior wine.

  • Attacks: usually a butt with their two sharp horns. Sometimes (20%) they use magic weapons.
  • Pipes: only 1 satyr per band is likely to have pipes, which only a satyr can properly play, and it is quite likely to play a tune first. Everyone within 6” who hears must save versus magic or be charmed, put to sleep, or made afraid (cause fear). If there are comely females in the group, the piping is to charm; if the intruder is fairly harmless, to sleep (and choice items are stolen from the sleepers); if the party is powerful, to cause fear. A creature that saves against any piping is unaffected by more music from the same pipes.
  • Stealth: very quiet, with keen senses: surprised only on a 1, and able to blend into foliage so as to be 90% undetectable to creatures unable to see hidden or invisible things.
  • Languages: their own tongue, elvish (understood only by sylvan elves), and common. Satyrs living near centaurs are 80% likely to be friendly with them, cooperating and speaking their language.

Description: skin of the upper body tan to light brown; hair elsewhere medium, reddish, or dark brown. Horns and hooves are black.

Giant scorpions are vicious predators. These adaptable mutations are found even in fairly cold places such as dungeons, and are likely to attack any creature that approaches.

  • Attacks: it tries to grab prey with its huge pincers while its segmented tail lashes forward to sting. The sting does 1-4 points of damage per hit, and the victim dies at once if it fails a poison saving throw. It can fight up to 3 opponents at once.
  • Its poison kills it if it accidentally stings itself.
  • It drags creatures it kills to its lair to eat.

Sea hags live in thickly overgrown shallows in warm seas; a very rare kind lives in fresh water. They are reclusive and hate beauty, so their lairs are likely to be in very dismal, ugly places. A sea hag quickly devours any victim.

  • Ghastly sight: so ghastly-looking that a creature seeing one is weakened by fright, losing half its strength for 1-6 turns, unless it saves versus magic.
  • Deadly glance: worse, 3 times per day she can cast a glance up to 3” that kills any creature failing its saving throw versus poison.

Giant sea horses are plant-eating sea creatures found in all but the coldest waters. They are naturally shy and avoid contact, but can be trained as steeds; aquatic elves and locathah sometimes capture and train them. In combat a sea horse butts with its head. The most common size is 2 hit dice; 30% have 3 and 10% have 4.

Sea lions are fearsome meat-eaters of coastal waters. They hunt in packs, giving loud bellowing roars even underwater. They attack with their clawed forelimbs and their jaws. Their maned heads are armor class 5, but thick scales make the rest of their body armor class 3. Since they often drag prey to their lair, valuables are sometimes left there. Young sea lions can be tamed and trained for guarding and hunting.

These horrible undead are found among ancient ruins or deep underground. They exist mainly on the negative material plane, so merely touching an opponent drains strength. They attack living things without hesitation to gain their life force.

  • Touch: their chill touch does 2-5 hit points of damage, and each hit also drains 1 point of strength. A human reduced to 0 strength or hit points has his life force drained and becomes a shadow. Lost strength returns 2-8 turns after the touch.
  • Immunities: sleep, charm, and hold spells and cold attacks do not affect them.
  • Hard to see: they look like nothing more than their name, so they are 90% undetectable. In bright light (such as from a continual light spell) they can be clearly seen.

Shambling mounds, or “shamblers”, are found in dismal marshes and certain wet underground places. Though it looks like a heap of rotting vegetation, it is actually an intelligent plant, usually 6’ to 9’ tall, about 6’ around at the base and 2’ at the top. It feeds on any living material through its weird roots and tendrils.

  • Attack: it attacks fearlessly, clubbing with its limbs twice per melee round. If both hit the same opponent, the victim is entangled and suffocates in its slime in 2-8 melee rounds unless the shambler is killed.
  • Toughness: its brain is in its middle, and its thick fibrous layers make its only vital area hard to reach, so most hits do little damage (armor class 0).
  • Defenses: being wet and slimy, it is unaffected by fire. Lightning makes it grow (add 1 hit die). Cold does half or no damage because of its plant nature. All weapons do only half damage, and it can flatten itself, so crushing has little effect. Spells that affect plants work on it; plant control and charm plant are good examples.
system.hpNote: Lightning makes it grow: add 1 hit die (MM p.87).

system.description:
Sharks of all kinds roam the oceans and seas, always moving and looking for food to satisfy their voracious appetites. A shark is a killing machine, attacking any recognizable food at any time.

  • Senses: noise (pressure changes) draws them from a mile or more, and they smell blood from at least as far.
  • Frenzy: any creature that looks hurt is 90% likely to be attacked, and a wounded one always is. This sends all nearby sharks into a frenzy in which they attack anything remotely like food. They seize prey, tear off a mouthful if it is not bite-sized, swim away to swallow it, and come back for more.
  • Weaknesses: ramming attacks, such as dolphins make, are especially dangerous to them, rupturing the internal organs that let them swim. A motionless shark dies in 2-5 melee rounds.

Giant shark (megalodon): giant white sharks and prehistoric sharks range from 20’ to 50’, the largest being prehistoric. They differ from their smaller kin only in being able to swallow large things whole, to match their other large-size advantages. A creature swallowed whole has 6 melee rounds to free itself by attacking; if it cuts its way out (reducing the shark to 0 hit points) in that time, it does not die. Each attack from inside has a cumulative −1 per round on damage (−1 in the 1st round, −2 in the 2nd, etc.).

Sharks of all kinds roam the oceans and seas, always moving and looking for food to satisfy their voracious appetites. A shark is a killing machine, attacking any recognizable food at any time.

  • Senses: noise (pressure changes) draws them from a mile or more, and they smell blood from at least as far.
  • Frenzy: any creature that looks hurt is 90% likely to be attacked, and a wounded one always is. This sends all nearby sharks into a frenzy in which they attack anything remotely like food. They seize prey, tear off a mouthful if it is not bite-sized, swim away to swallow it, and come back for more.
  • Weaknesses: ramming attacks, such as dolphins make, are especially dangerous to them, rupturing the internal organs that let them swim. A motionless shark dies in 2-5 melee rounds.

Giant shark (megalodon): giant white sharks and prehistoric sharks range from 20’ to 50’, the largest being prehistoric. They differ from their smaller kin only in being able to swallow large things whole, to match their other large-size advantages. A creature swallowed whole has 6 melee rounds to free itself by attacking; if it cuts its way out (reducing the shark to 0 hit points) in that time, it does not die. Each attack from inside has a cumulative −1 per round on damage (−1 in the 1st round, −2 in the 2nd, etc.).

Shedu travel the world furthering the ends of lawful good and helping allied creatures in need.

  • Attacks: they can attack with their powerful front hooves, but are more likely to use their psionic abilities: 3 major and 5 minor disciplines, all at 9th level of mastery.
  • Travel: they can become ethereal at will, and often travel the astral and ethereal planes.
  • Speech: their own language and most human tongues; with a limited telepathy, they usually communicate by direct mind contact.

Shriekers are mindless fungi that can move about and are normally quiet. They live in dark places underground. Light within 30’ or movement within 10’ makes them give a piercing shriek lasting 1-3 melee rounds, which has a 50% chance of attracting wandering monsters each round after. Purple worms and shambling mounds greatly prize shriekers as food.

Skeletons are undead monsters animated by the magic of a powerful evil magic-user or cleric. They obey their animator’s commands, which can be no more than a dozen or two words. They are found only in burial places, dungeons, and similar forsaken places, and attack until destroyed.

  • Attacks: some kind of weapon, but whatever the weapon, a hit does 1-6 hit points.
  • Weapons against them: sharp and/or edged weapons (spears, daggers, swords) do only half damage; blunt weapons (clubs, maces, flails, etc.) do normal damage. Fire does normal damage.
  • Immunities: sleep, charm, hold, and cold-based spells do not affect them.
  • Holy water: 2-8 hit points of damage per vial that hits.

Giant skunks are forest-dwelling animals that eat both plants and meat, and are quite willing to raid human camps for food.

  • Musk: facing any serious threat, it backs toward the opponent. If the other creature does not quickly get more than 6” away, the skunk sprays a cloud of vile musk 2” wide by 2” high by 6” long.
  • Effects: a creature failing to save versus poison is blinded for 1-8 hours. Either way, the musk makes it retreat a full move and lose 50% of both strength and dexterity from nausea for 2-8 turns.
  • Stench: any creature touched by the musk stinks disgustingly, and other creatures shun it. All cloth rots and becomes useless, including magical clothing that fails its saving throw. Creatures and non-cloth clothing and equipment must be washed and aired for several days to be completely rid of the stench.

This transparent monster is almost impossible to discover (5% chance of spotting it). It lives in dungeons and other dark places. It does not usually attack at once (10% chance); instead it follows its chosen victim to where the victim sleeps, and strikes only when its prey is asleep.

  • Movement: its semi-fluid body flows through openings as small as a rat hole or a large crack under a door.
  • Attack: by touching its prey’s bare flesh. Its secretions paralyze the victim unless he saves versus paralyzation. Once the victim is helpless, the tracker draws all the plasma from its body in 6 turns.

Giant slugs avoid light, preferring the depths of dungeons and similar places. Their rasping tongues let them eat substances such as wood and burrow through very hard earth. Despite their great bulk, having no bones lets them squeeze through very narrow or low openings. Their thick, rubbery hide and tremendous power let them break down doors easily.

  • Acid: they can bite with effect, but their main weapon is highly corrosive acid saliva, spat accurately over long distances. Normal range is 6”, with a base 50% chance to hit; each 1” closer adds 10%, and each 1” beyond 6” subtracts 10%.
  • First spit: always inaccurate, with only a 10% chance of hitting. Once it has found the range, later attacks have normal chances.
  • Weak spot: being so large, they can sometimes be caught in a narrow corridor where they cannot turn, and then attacked from behind and often slain without loss.
  • Weapons: their size and structure make blunt weapons useless; they must be attacked with edged weapons or by magic.

Description: pale gray, with a dead white underbelly.

Giant snakes may be found in any climate except the coldest. All eat meat.

Amphisbaena: it has a head at each end, both with poisonous fangs. It travels by gripping one of its necks and rolling like a hoop. It can attack with both heads, and a victim bitten who fails to save versus poison dies at once. Cold attacks do not harm it.

Constrictor: it usually drops coils from above, grabs prey in its coils, bites, and then squeezes for 2-8 points of damage per melee round. Several strong creatures (such as 4 humans of 16 or more strength) gripping it at head and tail can uncoil it in 2-5 melee rounds. After eating, it sleeps for several days.

Poisonous: giant poisonous snakes need no long explanation. Some kinds are worth noting, though, since their poison is so strong that even a victim who saves takes up to 3-18 hit points of damage.

Spectres are very powerful undead humans existing mainly on the negative material plane. They haunt the most desolate places, tombs, and dungeons. They hate sunlight and living things; daylight makes them powerless, and life makes them mourn their unlife.

  • Touch: its chilling touch does 1-8 hit points of damage and, through its negative force, drains 2 life energy levels. So an 11th-level character, or an 11 hit dice creature, struck by a spectre takes 1-8 hit points plus the loss of level ability, hit dice, etc. The loss is permanent, though characters can of course regain lost levels by earning more experience points, and certain magic might restore them.
  • Immunities: sleep, charm, hold, and cold-based spells do not affect them, nor do poison or paralyzation.
  • Holy water: 2-8 hit points of damage per vial that hits.
  • Raise dead: destroys a spectre unless it saves versus magic.
  • Victims: a human totally drained of life energy by a spectre becomes a half-strength spectre controlled by the one that drained him.

Sphinxes live only in warm climates. The different kinds have quite different traits.

Androsphinx: the male sphinx is very powerful and large. It attacks with its two great paws in melee, and can use cleric spells as a 6th-level human cleric. Androsphinxes usually shun gynosphinxes, resenting the females’ greater intelligence and neutral alignment. They speak all the sphinx languages and the common tongue of mankind.

Roars (three times per day, heard for several miles). It must be roused and angry to give the first, very angry to roar again, and infuriated to give the third.

  1. All creatures within 36” must save versus fear (as a wand) or flee in panic for 3 turns.
  2. Louder still: creatures within 20” must save versus petrifaction or be paralyzed with fright for 1-4 melee rounds. Creatures within 3” are also deafened for 2-12 melee rounds unless ogre-sized or larger (or with protected hearing).
  3. Creatures within 24” must save versus magic or lose 2-8 points of strength for as many melee rounds. Any creature within a 3” hemisphere of its mouth is knocked over unless ogre-sized or larger; those knocked over must save versus dragon breath or be stunned for 2-12 melee rounds, and those not knocked over take 2-16 hit points of damage (unless they are lions or part lion). The force also cracks stone within 3” unless the stone saves versus petrifaction.

Criosphinx: ram-headed, likely to be found in wooded areas. They prize wealth and usually try to extort passers-by, offering safe passage for a hefty bribe. In combat they attack with their two forepaws or a great butt of their horned head. They lust after gynosphinxes, who find them detestable. They speak their own tongue and that of andro- and gynosphinxes, and can speak with animals.

Gynosphinx: the female counterpart of the androsphinx, both knowledgeable and wise. Being neutral and prizing gems and similar wealth, they help humans only if paid, though they sometimes accept payment in riddles, poetry, prose, knowledge, or the location of an androsphinx. If not paid, the sphinx does not hesitate to devour the offender(s).

  • Once per day each: detect magic, read magic, read languages, detect invisible, locate object, dispel magic, clairaudience, clairvoyance, remove curse, and legend lore.
  • Once per week each: each of the symbols.
  • They speak all the languages the males know.

Hieracosphinx: hawk-headed, evil and greedy, found in hilly regions. They prefer warm-blooded prey, with humans high on the list of favorite meals, and attack with forepaws and beak each melee round. Like other sphinxes they value treasure highly. They have been known to serve as steeds for certain evil and powerful creatures.

Spiders are found in all regions except frigid ones, though legends tell of giant, fur-clad white spiders in polar lands. They live above and below ground. All are aggressive predators, and even when not hungry they attack creatures that disturb their web.

Giant spider: web builders, spinning their sticky traps horizontally or vertically to catch any creature that touches them; some lurk above a path to drop on prey.

  • Web: as tough and clinging as a web spell. A creature with 18 or more strength breaks free in 1 melee round, 17 strength in 2, etc. Webs burn easily.
  • Bite: poisonous; the victim must save versus poison or be killed.
  • It flees from a superior foe, usually hiding in some secret spot.

Huge spider: usually not a web builder but a roving hunter like a wolf spider, leaping 3” on prey to deliver its deadly bite. Others of this kind make carefully hidden lairs and rush out at prey (huge trapdoor spiders). They surprise prey on 1-5 (out of 6), and all saves against their poison are at +1.

Large spider: they scuttle and scurry about on walls, ceilings, and floors, in and out of their webs, always looking for victims, and are 90% likely to attack any creature within 3”. Their poison is usually fairly weak, so saves are at +2.

Phase spider: it looks like nothing more than a very great spider, but is far more. When attacking or attacked it can shift out of phase with its surroundings, coming back only when ready to bite. Victims save at −2 against its poison. Out of phase it is immune to nearly all attacks, but a phase door spell keeps one in phase for 7 melee rounds, and oil of etherealness and armor of etherealness put their wearers in the same phase as the spider when it shifts. Its webs equal a giant spider’s. It tries to avoid unfavorable encounters.

Giant water spider: fresh-water spiders found only in large lakes. They build great air-filled nests among underwater plants, with a clever airlock that lets them pass freely without losing the air. They run along the bottom or up and down plant or rock surfaces underwater, snatch passing prey, bite with poison, and take the victim to their lair to drain it at leisure. Being semi-intelligent, they can be approached with offerings of food, and water creatures such as nixies are sometimes friendly with them. Abandoned water spider lairs make excellent refuges for air-breathers.

A rare kind of water spider, twice the size of these, lives in salt water.
